item.title: [Bits + Bips] Could OpenAI Go Bankrupt While AI Takes Over the World?
item.dc:creator: Bits + Bips
item.content:encoded:
💡 创造性洞见

一个被忽略的反转：AI 时代的"炼金术陷阱"

这段讨论最耐人寻味的不是"OpenAI 会不会破产"，而是嘉宾们无意中揭示了一个反直觉的结构性真相：前沿模型公司可能正在扮演 19 世纪加州淘金热中淘金者的角色——而真正富起来的，是卖铲子的 Levi Strauss（牛仔裤）和 Wells Fargo（运输）。Chris 脱口而出的 "Picks and shovels" 不是比喻，而是一个精确的历史重演诊断。

但真正令人意外的是：这一次"卖铲人"也在变。 Zuckerberg 多年来被华尔街痛骂的"compute 执念"，在这个框架下不再是败家，而是一种"反向护城河"——不是通过知识产权或网络效应，而是通过物理原子的囤积。换句话说，Meta 可能正在用一种"中世纪城堡逻辑"（厚墙、储粮、储水）取代硅谷传统的"威尼斯贸易逻辑"（轻资产、网络、流动）。这是科技行业 30 年来第一次重新发现"重资产"的价值。

跨域连接：这不是科技泡沫，这是制药行业

主持人用 90 年代互联网泡沫做类比，但我认为更贴切的类比是制药行业，而这个连接几乎没人提到： - 烧钱研发前沿分子（= 训练前沿模型） → 90% 的候选药物失败 - 真正赚钱的不是发现分子的公司，而是 CRO（合同研究组织）、仪器制造商、原料药供应商（= NVIDIA、台积电、CoreWeave） - 监管最终塑造了寡头格局（FDA 审批壁垒 = Chris 预言的 AI 监管护城河） - 仿制药崛起侵蚀原研药利润（= 中国开源权重模型、Qwen、Muse 对 OpenAI 的侵蚀）

如果这个类比成立，那么 OpenAI 的终局不是成为 Google，而是成为辉瑞——一家周期性烧钱、依赖专利保护、不断被仿制药挤压、估值剧烈波动的公司。这比"下一个苹果"的叙事要悲观得多，也现实得多。

隐藏的系统性真相："分布式智能"正在吞噬"中心化智能"

Brian Armstrong 用 Qwen 自训反欺诈模型的那个细节，被嘉宾一笔带过，但它其实是整段讨论里最具爆炸性的信号。它意味着：

  • 智能正在从"公共事业"变成"自来水井"。当年每个工厂都有自己的蒸汽机，后来被电网取代；现在的趋势是反向的——企业开始重新"挖自己的井"，因为通用水（通用模型）既昂贵又无法针对内部数据优化。
  • 这与AWS 当年的叙事完全相反。云计算的逻辑是集中化规模经济；而私有化调优模型的逻辑是"数据重力"大于"算力重力"——你的数据在哪里，模型就应该在哪里训练。

最意外的推论：如果这个趋势成立，那么 OpenAI 的 API 业务本质上是一个"过渡性产品"，就像 2005 年提供"托管邮件服务器"的公司——现在都没了。真正的护城河不在模型本身，而在模型 + 专有数据 + 领域 workflow 的三位一体。而这恰恰是 OpenAI 最弱的一环，因为它没有一个"原生领域"。

一个让人脊背发凉的推断：讨论中那句"OpenAI 破产但 AI 接管世界"的玩笑，可能不是玩笑，而是AI 时代最可能的默认结局——因为智能这种商品，一旦被证明可以生产，就一定会被商品化，而商品化就是品牌溢价的坟墓。

📝 转录文本

开场与频道公告

If you've enjoyed Bits N' Bips these last few years, be sure to subscribe to its dedicated channels. All Bits N' Bips content has now moved to the Bits N' Bips channel and no longer plays on Unchained. Search Bits plus sign Bips wherever you listen and subscribe. We'll see you there.

OpenAI 的 "200 亿营收缺口" 报道

So, there was reporting that OpenAI, quote unquote, has a 20 billion revenue gap. Um, and it mainly arose from an attempt to produce a direct comparison with Anthropic, which is booking revenue from AWS and Google Cloud sales, according to Reuters. Um, because Anthropic's quarterly revenue topped OpenAI's for the first time in Q2, OpenAI is now saying it will reach 70 billion by year end. It is raising 30 billion ahead of an IPO in 2027.

Axios is saying in public markets investors will prefer actual revenue rather than financial constructs that are far more appropriate for early stage startups. Obviously, the market didn't like this. Oracle down, Nvidia down, CoreWeave down, chip makers overall down. Um, AI pivoting miners were sliding and the question is — is it accounting or is it demand?

把问题拆成三个独立问题

But I want to use this as a vector to look at a bigger problem, Chris, that you're raising here, which is: where are the economic gains from AI going to show up, period, full stop? And I think this is similar, if you've studied history of financial markets, to some of the problems that we had with attribution in the tech bubble.

Right? Because you really got to take three different questions apart and people like to compact them into a single ball and you should not. And those questions are:

  1. Is AI net valuable to the economy?
  2. If so, to whom is it valuable?
  3. And then on what timeline?

And I don't think your answer has to be "OpenAI is the winner" to believe that it's net valuable and on some timeline that will win, because as you said, it's driving significant demand for chips.

竞争格局：Meta、Gemini、Muse

And if you want an alternative model for AI, Meta just continues to ship, ship, ship, ship, ship with news. And by the way, to anybody not looking at the news, Gemini's Argon 4 allegedly is doing very well on benchmarks. I haven't seen it publicly yet. But Muse 1 just hit today and is basically touching the capabilities or even exceeding them of OpenAI's latest models and like Claude.

And so if that's true, I have a lot of questions about where the economic winners are. Is frontier modeling essentially a game where you're just constantly burning money and never have a moat? And so it's actually other stuff that will accrue the value?

So, Chris, I want to throw the ball back to you. You've thought about this a lot as a venture investor. You're now at Franklin Templeton. If we're seeing a world in which chips demand is insatiable, the frontier model companies continue to incinerate money and while revenue is growing, the money incineration is not slowing down. And you've got competitors in the water doing, call it, orthogonal things like the Chinese open weight labs or Meta — how do you make sense of this whole picture?

Chris 的回答：等待监管构建寡头护城河

You wait for regulation.

And what regulation does is it forces you into probably like a duopoly or a duopoly plus. That's the natural state of mature markets. Um, if you get that regulation which you're hoping for, maybe it can take care of some of your liability issues, maybe not. But what it will do is it will create a material moat which will allow you to — when you have regulation, it forces everyone to have the same fixed costs. And what it does is it squeezes margin and forces scale. And usually not that many folks can compete.

So, that's why you see them so focused on this because that is the end game. It's where you have that regulatory moat, where there's a couple folks that are scaled. Think about the different industries, you know, Pepsi, Coke — you just see it happen over and again, particularly with regulated industries. Now, maybe it's not two, maybe it's like three or four, whatever, but that keeps out the competition. That's probably the end game that they're seeking.

And look, there's a lot of folks that are very focused on regulation. I go back to what we talked about previously with hacking. There are laws. New technology doesn't change the law. Like you still got to follow the law, but for some reason every time we throw new technology out, we're like, "Oh, no, no, the law doesn't apply. It doesn't matter. You can go hack and rip people off and..."

So, I think, you know, maybe those laws adapt over time, maybe the regulations adapt over time, but until that point, we have laws. So, yeah, maybe that's the end game here — is we get that regulation, and then there's just the compression of fees and scaling out.

硬件与算力：物理护城河

For me, I think part of what I'm looking at here is: it may be the case that the winners in this space are the people provisioning the hardware and the compute capacity. Like this is an inversion of some of the previous things we've seen, but it may be that the physical atoms become the driver of this, right?

One of the things, you know, with plenty of investors yelling at him about it, that Zuckerberg has been focused on is just compute, compute, compute, compute — and he's been focused on that for years. And now they have a moat. And that moat is not regulation, it's physical capacity.

So, 100%. I mean, Compute's not going away anytime soon, my man. And if anything, maybe you see it getting changed when we have the quantum systems online — and there's a lot of investment going in there as well.

一个大胆预测："OpenAI 可能破产，但 AI 接管世界"

Yeah, it's creating this framework where you need to have bet not just on something on the frontier, but the right thing on the frontier — because I see a totally plausible future where 5 years forward OpenAI is bankrupt, Anthropic is bankrupt, and AI is taking over the world.

Picks and shovels, my man. Picks and shovels.

Exactly. It is a totally possible outcome that NVIDIA remains a winner. You know, Meta is a winner, Google is a winner, right? Data services becomes the thing that wins.

专业化模型与碎片化趋势

And the other part that's really interesting to me about this is: we're starting to see more model tuning and specialized models. So, to pull on two threads:

  • In the Muse drop for Muse Wonder today, they had a specifically tuned legal model, right? They're starting to use that — it is increasing specialization within these frontier models.
  • Brian Armstrong was tweeting about tuning an instance of Qwen, which is Alibaba's open weight model, where they were able to host that themselves, train it on Coinbase data, and greatly improve fraud detection.

So, it may also be that it's not so much — call it — moving the entire frontier, because that takes more and more and more parameters and ever more complex models, but instead starting to specialize the models for specific tasks and making them more agile. And this kind of goes back to what we saw with the development of the internet in general, right? Things start to fragment, things start to specialize. It's not the all-singing, all-dancing everything that wins.

分发（Distribution）才是关键

I see in that last set of comments you're able to channel Ron and say something about OpenAI — and, you know, out of deference to him. But look, I'm not as down on OpenAI as you guys are apparently.

Well, my point is, look, do I see worlds in which they succeed? Yes. I think what's understated is I also see plenty of worlds in which they fail. Go back and look at the '90s at all the big tech names and how many made it to today.

Yeah, but — that's a comment specific to OpenAI. It's just hard to predict the distribution of future outcomes.

Yeah, but value does accrue to applications and those applications that win, win. And so, it's still early. We'll see what happens.

That's true, but a lot of that's distribution. All right, so on that note —

Wait, Austin, do they have distribution?

Do they?

How does OpenAI not have distribution? How many users do they have?

I mean, they have an app and they have tens of millions of users. I agree with that level, but that is a disruptable level of users. They are not like Apple, which has billions of users locked in.

That's fair. Yeah, and 100%. And they were quick to start disrupting Google when they came out. I remember all of a sudden I started using ChatGPT instead of Google and I was like, wait a second. Um, you're right — this stuff can move quickly in either direction.

Um, and what are we seeing from a value perspective? Distribution. Distribution rules. As time marches forward, I think more value is being accrued to distribution — more and more every single day. If you've got distribution, it's valuable.

结语与赞助

If you liked this segment, please like, subscribe, and tune in every Monday at 4:30 p.m. Eastern Time. I'm Austin Campbell, the host of Bips and Bips, along with my friends Rom Allawalia and Chris Perkins, and our slate of exceptional guests. Every week, we're going to discuss macro, crypto, and the collision of worlds, covering topics that move markets and shape the financial landscape.

One more thing. We've got a listener survey open. It takes just a few minutes. It's anonymous, and it changes what we make next. Use the QR code on screen or go to unchainedcrypto.com/survey. The link is in the show notes.

What if your crypto could do more than just sit in your wallet? Nexo is a digital assets wealth platform where you can generate daily interest on your crypto or borrow funds against your assets. Today, Nexo serves more than 10 million clients. Find out more at nexo.com.

item.title: [投资TALK君] 突击直播：通胀炸裂，AI泡沫
item.dc:creator: 投资TALK君
item.content:encoded:
💡 创造性洞见

一、通胀数据的"参与率"隐喻——市场最被忽略的二阶指标

大多数人盯着 CPI/PPI 的头条数字，但真正值得关注的是 Powell 在 Jackson Hole 讲话中提到的 Diffusion Index（扩散指数）。这是一个精妙的类比：通胀的"宽度"而非"高度"才是美联储真正害怕的东西。

这里有一个让人意外的跨领域连接——Diffusion Index 的本质，与股市中的"市场广度（Market Breadth）"是同一种数学结构。当标普指数被七巨头拉到新高、但下跌股票数多于上涨股票时，分析师会说"这是不健康的上涨"。反过来，当 CPI 总体数据爆表、但只有少数项目贡献涨幅时，Powell 会说"这是可以接受的通胀"。

惊人的对称性：美联储看通胀的方式，和老练的交易员看指数的方式，用的是同一种统计直觉——不要被加权平均欺骗，要去看分布本身的形状。这意味着，一个合格的宏观分析师和一个合格的技术分析师，大脑里跑的其实是同一个算法。

二、CoreWeave 的 15% 收益率——一个被整个市场误读的"幸存者偏差"

市场在恐慌 CoreWeave 老债券的 15% 收益率，仿佛这就是未来融资成本。但这里藏着一个彻底的逻辑陷阱：15% 是过去发的债在当前市场定价下的到期收益率，而不是未来增量融资的成本。两者完全不是等号。

更有趣的是，老黄主导的新型融资结构——用 Meta 的信用背书来给 CoreWeave 的数据中心融资——其底层逻辑与政府基建中的 PPP（Public-Private Partnership，公私合营）项目融资一模一样。这是一个绝妙的跨领域套用：

  • 政府修医院/高速：政府信用担保未来 20-30 年现金流 → 承包商拿着这个担保去发私募债 → 融资成本接近主权利率
  • Meta 建数据中心：Meta 承诺长期租赁现金流 → CoreWeave 拿着这个订单做结构化融资 → 融资成本接近 Meta 的信用利差

那个让人意外的洞见是：AI 基础设施的融资结构，正在悄悄地把自己从"科技风投"重塑为"类主权基建"。这意味着市场在用错误的估值框架给它定价——用的是科技股的 PE 和债券的 YTM，但它真实的现金流形态更像一条收费公路。当市场终于意识到这件事时，重估会非常剧烈。

三、"脑力劳动"向"体力需求"的能量守恒——一个被忽视的消费转移命题

Kevin 顺口提到一个点：如果 AI 替代了脑力工作，释放的时间会转化为"对实际消费的欲望"。这句话被埋在最后，但它可能是整场直播最深刻的洞见。

这里有一个反直觉的类比——想想自动化出现后家务时间的悖论：洗衣机、洗碗机、吸尘器节省了数百小时家务时间，但调查显示现代人花在"家庭管理"上的时间没有减少，只是转移到了"情感劳动"、"育儿管理"、"消费决策"上。能量没有消失，只是改变了形态。

AI Agent 替代脑力劳动后，释放出的"认知带宽"不会蒸发，它会流向两个方向： 1. 向身体消费流动——旅游、餐饮、线下体验、健身——这解释了为什么电力行业工资暴涨、服务业需求结构会扭曲 2. 向身体型 AI（具身智能/机器人） 流动——因为大脑一旦被服务，身体马上会提出要求

所以 Universal Basic Income 的真正触发点，不是失业率飙升，而是消费结构的 K 型分化加速到临界点——当"超人"（会用 AI 的人）的消费溢出到实体服务业，而被替代者的购买力崩塌时，政治层面的 UBI 会从边缘话题变成不可避免的议题。这是一个"AI 革命通过消费侧而非生产侧触发社会结构重构"的另类预言。

📝 转录文本

开场

Hello, can you hear me? Hello. I see someone is here. Can you hear me? You can hear me. Okay.

Why did you come to the live stream this morning? There are two reasons. The first reason is that I didn't make a video yesterday. I did a live stream on the app yesterday. The live stream itself was only for members, but I made it public later. But I guess many people who watched my video in the post office may not have participated in yesterday's live stream.

But after the live stream, there will be a live stream. So I want to take this opportunity to talk about some questions that everyone was concerned about yesterday. I'll pick some questions and talk about them. It won't be too long. It's 45 minutes and an hour. I'll take the time I know there are many questions about the shares and the red-line. So I think it's better to start with some of your questions and then we can discuss some of them.

I want to talk about two things.

一、通胀数据：PPI 与 CPI 的解读

1. 当下通胀与 2021 年的类比

The first is the inflation data. Yesterday's inflation data and today's PPI data. These two data, no matter from which angle you explain it, are not a good set of data. So we need to keep observing.

The inflation data is not good. It brought our memory back to 2021. In April and May of 2021, the data of the second-hand car was not very good. Then the data of the second-hand car began to spread to some other inflation projects. The most important thing was the ECI data in November. It's not just the ECI in November. The ECI is announced once per quarter. If you go back to August, the ECI has actually been rising from May and August. By November, it will be a direct turning point for the US Fed to let the ECI data be a turning point.

But if we look at the growth of wages now, the ECI is the growth of wages. But if we look at the growth of wages now, we don't see it. So, although the unemployment rate is high in the labor market, and the increase in the data on the big capital is not high, the labor market is balanced. We don't see a very tight labor market, nor do we see the growth of wages.

So, up to now, I think although the data we just published in the past month is not good, it is not satisfied with us entering 2022. If I see any rise in ECI data, I will be more careful. By then, I might go back and think about the red-light against the wind and the wind on the basic surface. Which wind is stronger? Or, as I've always said, is it EPS or PE that can win over PE? Or can PE win over EPS?

So far, I still think from this year to now, it's the same. EPS is basically a main line. I think EPS will still be a main line. The basic face of the company, the landing of AI, is still a main line.

2. 美联储真正在看什么：Diffusion Index

So this is the inflation data. In addition, I would like to add a little bit about inflation data. My point of view has always been that inflation data itself is not that important. What matters is the sentiment of the US Federal Reserve on inflation data. Because for the market, the reason why the market is doing this feedback on the PPI data is because the market expects the US dollar to do this.

But the data from the past month, if there is any talk from June, July, August, or September to now, if there is any key takeaway, it's from the August Jackson meeting to the August 9th meeting. In the August Jackson meeting, he talked about called the Diffusion Index of inflation.

If you separate all the inflation projects, there are hundreds of them. If you separate all of them, you can see how much the annual inflation rate is at 3% or more. The annual inflation rate is the increase in the rate. If the rate increases, it means that the inflation rate is expanding. The range of inflation is getting higher and higher. But if the proportion of inflation is slowly decreasing, that is, the data we saw in the past two months, the inflation has not expanded.

This is the second-order effect that the Fed is talking about. It doesn't want to see a rise in oil prices, and then because of that, other inflation will gradually expand. This is not what the Fed wants to see. So this diffusion index, the data from the past two months is not that high. It's a decline. Although the final result of the inflation is expected to be higher.

How can we understand it? I made an analogy yesterday. You can understand it as the index is breaking high because the previous seven major tech stocks brought the index to break high, but the participation rate of the entire market is declining. Can you understand? So what Mr. Kevin said is that I see the participation rate. If the participation rate is like this, if the participation rate drops, I can accept it. If the participation rate goes up, I think the mood is too high or the turnover is too high. You should be able to understand this kind of analogy.

So this is the first point. What does the KMOS look at?

3. 美联储的"连续数据"思维

The second point, he emphasized many times, even if in September, the last choice is to add C, the CPI in September, the CPI data announced in August, is not important anymore. It's not important in his perspective because a group of CPI data is not a trend.

So the CPI data we just saw in September was released in October. The CPI data we just saw, including the PPI data released today, is indeed bad. There's no need to doubt it. Except for the Diffusion Index, from the perspective of participation, it's not that bad. Or it's actually still down from last month. But the data itself is bad.

So in this case, it's at least one-month data. If you connect the core PCs of the past three months, it should be 0.1, 0.25. I don't know about this data. And Nick didn't say it, and Anna Wong didn't say it. I guess because the PPI data is not good, it may be around 0.35. It's 0.1, 0.25, 0.35.

If the data for the next month is still very bad, then the holiday in December is basically quite low. That's what I think because it's a link. If the data for the next month drops again, for example, to 0.1 or 0.2, we can't create a trend again. So in December, it will be 50% or 50%. So basically, the data with a connection will be better. The way of thinking of the connection data will be better. It won't make the market feel that the data for a month will be very different.

So if we combine the Jacksonville meeting in August and the Fed meeting in September, I think it's been four months so far. For some of the companies in the Kaifeng Watch how to look at data or how to make some monetary policy decisions based on data. I think it's already clear and not vague. Especially in September, he reviewed what he talked about in the past three months. In fact, it is very related. It is actually predictable. But now with AI, after you solve the coding part, you will find that the space you can imagine, now, through coding, you can solve it in a week or a month. You can implement this idea. In the end, it's just about whether you can sell this idea or whether there are people who can help you.

四、Q&A：市场核心议题答疑

1. 关于 Besson 介入与市场自我调节

It's been a while since I last did a live stream. I haven't done one on a cruise ship for a long time. So I thought I'd give you some time this morning. I didn't make a video last night. In most cases, if the market is more scary, I will make a video. But I was too busy yesterday and I was a bit tired.

There are often some challenging questions. For example, when can I predict the turning point? I think these are all difficult questions. I don't think I can answer that.

Do you still think that Besson will intervene in the market? The market is already helping Besson. Whether Besson will come back or not is the same. It's about the purpose. If he has a purpose, he needs a result. If the market is helping him with the result, does it make any sense for him to intervene? Why? The market is too full. You can understand that in this position, the bond market has no more buyers. So the buyer, instead, in that position, the buyer appears as a normal interest rate, or the price appears to rise. This is the result. You can understand that in the market, we often see a good news in the stock market. Why? There is no buyer, no additional buyer. Or the consensus of the market is a base. Or there is a stage.

2. 美国衰退与 AI 泡沫

Many people are calling for the US to back down, and then to open up the AI bubble on the weekend. What do I think? If you often watch my videos, calm down a little bit, you won't be able to make these conclusions. I can't see any possibility of American recession. I think we have been from the beginning to the end.

First of all, what is the GDP of the recession? What is the composition of GDP? I said personal consumption, enterprise consumption, government consumption, import and export data. That's it. That's the idea. Import and export. Where do you look at personal consumption? Look at the financial statements of the US bank. 5% increase, the same rate increase. There is no sign of any consumption. Of course, this 5% is a... We call it the "wide-ranging light". If you go to the inflation, it's 1%. If it's real, consumption is 2%. Inflation is 3%. PC is 3%. Consumption is 5%. 5-2 is 3%. Consumption is 2%.

What is corporate investment? CapEx. Capital spending of big tech. Capital spending will slow down. But will capital spending have a negative growth? Can't see it. Why? Because I can't see the way of AI. I haven't seen the way of AI yet.

The consumption of these two ends accounts for more than 60% of GDP. If consumption still maintains this 2% increase, capital opening will still increase, but the increase will slow down. The increase must slow down, because it is impossible to repeat the same amount of volume. But the increase is still increasing. Next year, 20 years, compared to 2025, 50% of the possibility is very high. Two big companies have already been talked about.

The rest are the government's spending. The government's spending on imports and exports is a noise. If you put it aside, how will the US fall after you take control of two big companies? I can't see any US fall behind it. What will the increase in the cycle affect? You just pay attention to the US bank's financial statements. After the increase in the cycle, will the US consumption decrease? In fact, in this period, the oil price has been relatively high since the war. It has never been low for a very long time. Look at the consumption and the slowdown. Look at the consumption and slowdown of the entire US bank's financial statements. Although we say that consumers are now in a very K-economic situation, there is no way. When we look at the red line, you have to look at a relatively upper level. You have to look at it from a relatively higher perspective.

So I didn't see any signs of falling.

As for AI bubbles, I have already talked about it before. If you talk about bubbles, I think when we hear this kind of view, I'm not saying I'm right, but when we think about these issues or when we hear this kind of view, we can ask a question. I said that bubble itself is not suitable for demand and supply. You have to ask where the demand is and where the supply is. After you have talked about these two questions, you can get the conclusion whether there is bubble or whether bubble is broken. If you only talk about one question, you can't get a conclusion.

I talked about the question of call with before. If you only talk about the rise in financing costs, and not talk about the needs behind it, you won't get a call with whether this company will have a problem. You can't get this conclusion.

So if you only talk about the single-sided logic, trying to prove your own conclusion, you can't push B. Of course, I know a lot of people watching the video or listening to other people's opinions only want to know a conclusion, only want to know a result, and don't care about the process behind it. But if we want to think about it ourselves, we need to know the reasons in between, or what is the reason behind the UK relationship. We need to make a conclusion. The point of view of the arguments in the cause and effect is whether the perspective is comprehensive enough or just one-sided.

3. 关于 10 月是否降息

I forgot to talk about the increase in October. I talked about it on X. I talked about it after the CPI came out yesterday. I don't think it will increase in October. I still think it won't increase in October. I actually talked about why I don't think so.

One is that Kevin and I are still looking at it. He thinks... Of course, he will have a speech tonight in Thailand at 11:30. The time of the meeting is 11:30. One is that he won't... One-month data is not a trend. This is the most important point. The second point is the previous Diffusion Index. The data he saw actually had a decline. Of course, after the PPI data came out today, I don't know if it was PCIe. The prediction that Bloomberg made yesterday was that the Diffusion Index would fall. If these two data are added together, I think the probability of not adding is higher.

The other thing is the midterm elections. There is no need to add during the midterm elections. If you really think it's very, very urgent, first of all, it's not very urgent now. I remember once a member of the US National Party said that without urgency, there must be continuous adding. Who was it? John Williams. I forgot who it was.

If you are really in a hurry, you can add 50 points in December. We'll talk about it later. We'll start with the data. You can see a lot of data in December. If the data for the next three months is so high, adding 50 points in December is not impossible. It's possible. It's not impossible. If the data for the next few months is as high as the data for the next two months, like 0.3 or 0.4, if the data for the PC is 0.4, adding 50 points in December is possible. But now, I think we can only talk about the probability of the situation, because the data is evolving. It's a process of evolution. I think the probability situation is that it won't increase in October, and it will continue to increase in December.

4. 关于半导体与高通

The expected return of semiconductor has dropped. They went to the US market where the risk reward is better. Because someone talked about why the interest rate dropped and then the US stock dropped, and then the semiconductor dropped. The risk reward of the semiconductor has risen, but where did it go down? If the price drops, your risk reward will definitely rise, but it basically hasn't changed. You must answer why Qualcomm doesn't replace me.

Someone asked me, "I think in the next half to a year, I think Agents will be on the ground." Someone asked me to talk about the labels. I've talked about the labels in many ways. I said, "Agent is a private company." Before Meta was popular, I thought that the next private companies, Meta, Apple, Google, and Qualcomm, I've talked about this a lot, this 4.2% period. During this period, some people say that from the perspective of AEM, ARM might be better. We have to be stubborn on one side, and then the basic side is on one side. On the other side, I think it's also from a rest-a-live perspective.

I think why these two days, why this question seems to be completely unrelated to what I talked about earlier. It's actually related to why the high and low were not mentioned in the past two days. It's not how good the basic high and low are. But there are not many investment warehouses in Kaotong. There are not many panic warehouses or hedge funds warehouses in Kaotong. We thought that the market would be like a semiconductor. The retail investors must have contributed a part, but many of them also ran away from the institutions. After the headline news came out, some of the chain stores fell. Why didn't Kaotong fall? Because there were no investment warehouses in Kaotong, so they didn't fall. It's that simple.

So, I think this also shows that the market doesn't have any investment opportunities. This shows that these companies don't receive any attention from the market. It's not that they are not on the top. It's actually good. These signs are not surprising. They have fallen a lot. Right? These days, Intel has fallen a lot. AMD has fallen. And then, Marvel has fallen.

So, I think there are many standards. I talked about a lot of standards related to agent and the same with the smart system. But each standard says that the position of the investment group is different. The position is different and so is the position of the committee. I asked a lot of standards in the live broadcast yesterday. I said there are three companies. I'm still willing to add two companies. One is Google and the other is Qualcomm. The other one that I'm more and more optimistic about is the Microsoft I mentioned earlier. They are all smart devices. One is a B-turned smart device, the other is a C-turned smart device.

5. Intel 与管理层信心

Let's look for the next question. "Inter."

Many people asked me about Intel yesterday. I don't have many answers. I don't have anything to say. "The price is going up or down." When it goes up, you asked me about Intel. I can also say that I said this during my live stream yesterday.

If you go to see Intel, I think the number of interviews with Chen Liwu is quite high. The more I see this CEO, the more I think that this CEO is totally trustworthy. He is irresistible in terms of his connections, his execution, his actions, and his behavior. I've shared this before. In my perspective, there are many management layers that are almost indisputable.

Asmai. Actually, there are some features. Asmai is a company that you don't need to listen to their financial reports. You just need to give them the money. But it doesn't mean that the industry won't go through a cycle. It went through a cycle in 2022. In 2023, China's EUV was also built. Then there was a wave. In 2023 and 2024, there was a wave of decline. Then, now, it just broke through a historical high. Then there is Taichi. The financial report of Taichi store is not good. Every time the financial report data comes out, it is all B. Even after you and them go through the 22-year cycle, you will find that this is a management level that is completely trustworthy.

I think, of course, Intel has not experienced a cycle since it was established. But it always takes the company in a very correct direction. At that time, Intel was a market that thought that you completely missed the entire AI trade. But it was established that it didn't miss it. We will do edge AI in the future, including now smart objects and CPU. So I think Chen Lin is a completely trustworthy CEO. The entire management team, I think, is completely trustworthy.

So this type of company, I actually have a lot of confidence. Even if the stock price falls, I can have more confidence that the management team can bring it out. So, of course, you still need to match the warehouse position. If you say you want me to take the whole warehouse and then the backstop, I wouldn't be willing to accept it. I wouldn't be willing to take such a big wave of the overall warehouse position to accept such a fact or to accompany it to take such a big wave. So the warehouse position still needs to be controlled. But in the current situation of this warehouse position, if you say it will fall down 30, 40, 50, and then the backstop, I think I can accept it. And in the future, I'm willing to add more if it's just because the market is in a bad mood.

So I think I can share this. After I heard about this company's management team, I think his confidence is almost at the forefront.

6. 关于老马与存储价格

Can you tell me if Lao Ma is a black storage? Is it because Lao Ma took over the business? I don't know what his purpose is. I really don't know what his purpose is. It's not necessary. Maybe they will go to pressure other storage companies to lower prices. He said the US light is good. He praised the US light. I don't know.

I have updated SOX's forward P. You can go and check out the forward P of semiconductor. I updated it yesterday. I won't go into too much detail here.

I don't have much to say about the US light and storage. I think, first of all, from the financial report and orders, Lao Ma said, I said to Lao Ma that in 2028, China will make a lot of RAM. I said, "Lao Ma, think about it. When did you meet Lao Ma?" He said, "We never met."

I think... I don't know why he did that, but there must be a reason behind it. I don't know. I don't know why. I don't know why.

7. AI 替代人工后谁来消费？"超人"与 K 型经济

Okay, let's get to the last two questions. That's it for today. I'm not going to be live-streaming for too long. It's mainly for you to talk about inflation. I'll probably make a video at night. I'll make a video at night. Mainly to make up for the video I didn't make yesterday.

Okay, this question. If the agent falls, the unemployment rate rises, who will consume it? How do you support the company's profits? Isn't it already...

I think if everyone is retired and has financial freedom, we may only worry about how to invest in the future. If you are still like me, still like a bull, I think the future will be formed... This concept is not a new concept. In the past, you talked about superhuman. How do you define superhuman? How can AI do what you are doing now and give you the benefits? How can AI use AI to give you the benefits and generate greater value? Whether it's in your personal life, in your own business, or in your company, superhuman. Superhuman will be able to...

...and those who don't use AI or think AI is a terrible thing will be able to make a big difference. This is different from the blue collar workers in the 1980s, who were the industrial class. I think it's really different. You just have to make a living and pay for your dream in the US. But this time, it's really different. The K-shaped economy will only become more and more K-shaped.

I haven't finished talking about the alternative AI. From the perspective of the enterprise, they can choose two options. The first option is to hire. The second option is to keep the original AI and let the original AI do other things. To do some AI. From the perspective of enterprise operations, there are two options. One is to open a source and the other is to cut a flow. AI is the simplest way to decrypt. You need to do some repetitive tasks and then decrypt. Open source is actually what software companies are doing now.

Open source is also possible for traditional companies. You can arrange other jobs for the remaining employees. Those jobs can be related to your open source. You can do that. So from the company's perspective, the first step is to think directly about decrypting. How to use AI to decrypt and how to use AI to increase efficiency. The second step is probably to open a company.

Of course, this is a traditional company, but we still need to think about one thing. There will be many emerging companies, AI may create many other kinds of public sector. For example, the demand for data centers, but also the demand for electric power. This is a very... This is already a very popular public sector in the United States. Last time, when I was in the offline, I said that the electric power salary in the United States is one year. They said that the highest salary can reach 500,000. One year, 500,000 in Texas. At least, the average is about 200,000 to 300,000. So, it creates a lot of needs for other industries.

So, there will still be many new industries. But for the original companies, it depends on the management level of the company to make this decision. So, I think it's too early to think about this issue now. But in the future, is it possible to have the UBI, Universal Basic Income, as Lama said? I think it's possible. But I don't think we need to worry about that. We need to prepare ourselves for the future.

8. AI Agent 与物理机器人：从脑力到体力的下一步

Okay, the last question. Will AI Agents need to bind physical robots in the future to be so hard and hard to control?

Actually, this question follows the previous one. We're not talking about investment now, but we're mainly talking about the future of AI development. When AI can replace a lot of brain work, right? We call it bots.

You think about brain work, or we actually need to use our brains to go through a medium. For example, your personal intelligence. For example, I have to order a meal today. My brain says I have to order a meal. Then I use my hands, apps, and my phone to complete this order. It's a brain output. Of course, it's a part of the physical energy. But after you have a personal intelligence, this personal body can completely do this for you. You just need to make the next command. This is brain work.

The same goes for the B-shape. Most of your work is basically brain work. Most of your work, at least in the office, is brain work. So, brain work can be replaced by many AI. What can't be replaced is the physical, physical, physical...

Then maybe some of the public will, because you think if the brain public, many brain publics are replaced, in fact, it is increased, because you have time to come out, you may have a desire for the consumption of the actual demand, the demand may increase, the desire to consume may increase, more time, you must spend this time to go to other places, right? So, on the other hand, there may be some demands for non-brain, so the public may also rise. So part of the brain may go to the body.

Then when there is really physical AI, many physical AI, robots, and so on, then it's really a BI. You can still do it. AI is a nuclear bomb. I think we live in a stage where people are excited and panicked. You really don't know what stage AI can develop, but AI develops very, very fast. So, from an investment perspective and a personal perspective, I think we have to follow this pace. Otherwise, it will be completely eliminated. And this time being eliminated is accelerating the time and speed of the entire AI landing and development.

结束语

Okay, that's it for today. We should still have time for this at night. I will do a video for everyone at night. Today I said that I mainly didn't record the video yesterday, and then I helped everyone to make a video. Then I talked about a point that I want to pay attention to in the current market. Then call with, and then talk a little bit about the general data.

Okay, that's it for today. Bye bye.

item.description:
## 一、通胀数据的"参与率"隐喻——市场最被忽略的二阶指标
大多数人盯着 CPI/PPI 的头条数字，但真正值得关注的是 Powell 在 Jackson Hole 讲话中提到的 **Diffusion Index（扩散指数）**。这是一个精妙的类比：**通胀的"宽度"而非"高度"才是美联储真正害怕的东西**。
这里有一个让人意外的跨领域连接——Diffusion Index 的本质，与股市中的"**市场广度**（Market Breadth）"是同一种数学结构。当标普指数被七巨头拉到新高、但下跌股票数多于上涨股票时，分析师会说"这是不健康的上涨"。反过来，当 CPI 总体数据爆表、但只有少数项目贡献涨幅时，Powell 会说"这是可以接受的通胀"。
**惊人的对称性**：美联储看通胀的方式，和老练的交易员看指数的方式，用的是同一种统计直觉——**不要被加权平均欺骗，要去看分布本身的形状**。这意味着，一个合格的宏观分析师和一个合格的技术分析师，大脑里跑的其实是同一个算法。
## 二、CoreWeave 的 15% 收益率——一个被整个市场误读的"幸存者偏差"
市场在恐慌

item.title: [Lex Clips] Jensen Huang gets mobbed by engineers in Taiwan | Lex Fridman
item.dc:creator: Lex Clips
item.content:encoded:
💡 创造性洞见

一、Jensen 现象：硅片第一次拥有了"人格引力场"

视频里最震撼的不是技术，而是一位芯片 CEO 被工程师围堵的场景。这在半导体史上几乎没有先例——Intel 的 Grove、Krzanich、Gelsinger 走在街上没人认识；台积电张忠谋在西方几乎无面孔。而现在一个做 GPU 的黄仁勋，被叫做"Beatles"。

这背后藏着一个被忽略的转折：AI 让硅第一次"可见"。 过去三十年，芯片是一个"消失的产业"——它越成功，越不可见（埋在服务器里、嵌在手机里）。而生成式 AI 让每一次对话都能被追溯到"是哪块芯片在算"，于是硬件突然有了叙事权。黄仁勋不是靠营销成为明星的，他是第一个"被 token 抬起来"的硬件家。

跨领域连接：这其实复刻了 19 世纪末爱迪生-特斯拉时代的工程师崇拜——那也是基础设施（电）从不可见转向可见的时刻。每当底层能源被重新定义，底层能源的"面孔"就会被神化。你现在看到的 Jensenity，是算力即电力这个事实的社会化外显。

二、"The more you buy, the more you make" 不是销售话术，是经济学范式切换

Jensen 一句玩笑："The more you buy, the more you make." 看似销售技巧，但真正该震惊的是他顺手完成了一次经济学模型的替换：

  • x86 时代：CPU 卖的是"核"，经济学单位是 dollars per core——这是租金经济（Rent Economy），客户买的是"位置"，像买地皮。
  • AI 时代：GPU 卖的是"token"，经济学单位是 tokens per second——这是生产经济（Production Economy），客户买的是"产出速率"，像买织布机。

这个转变比它听起来剧烈得多——它意味着数据中心第一次有了"产能利用率"这个工业指标。过去数据中心是房地产（出租），现在是工厂（生产）。这也解释了为什么 Jensen 疯狂压缩组装时间（2 小时 → 5 分钟）：在租金经济里，建造慢没关系；在生产经济里，每多一天没建完，就是少卖的 token。

出人意料的一点：这其实复现了第一次工业革命的核心转折——从"土地租金"到"工厂产出"的价值计量切换。换句话说，黄仁勋不是在卖芯片，他是在给整个数字文明重装一次 18 世纪。

三、两个被埋没的"反直觉金句"——以及它们之间的隐秘共振

视频里有两句话被当成闲聊带过，但其实是贯穿 NVIDIA 工程哲学的核心：

"Things that are easy to build are also reliable."
"Speed is not everything. Sometimes you have to pause and think."

表面上，一句讲硬件，一句讲对话；但它们是同一个原理的两种投射：降低认知负荷 = 提升系统稳健性。

  • 一个 GPU 板子，如果组装步骤从 2 小时压到 5 分钟，不是因为"工人更快"，而是因为结构本身消除了可能出错的决策点——这叫 affordance design，是 Don Norman 认知心理学中的概念被硬件化。
  • 一个人，如果边说边想，就等于让"输出"和"推理"共享同一条带宽——这也是认知负荷过载。所以 Jensen 承认自己"打字能思考，说话不能"。

跨领域的意外连接：这和 Toyota 生产系统的 jidoka（自働化）原则、以及海军核反应堆的 Rickover 工程哲学完全同构——"易建造 = 高可靠"是一条自然律，不是软要求。而当 Jensen 把这条原则同时应用在钢板和自己的大脑上时，你看到的其实是同一个人把工业工程原理应用到了元认知。

四、最隐藏的一个信号：Wabi-sabi 时刻

视频里最容易被跳过的是他盯着一块（可能是有瑕疵的）芯片或样品说：

"When I was young, I would think that's not good. But now, I love wabi-sabi."

一个把 "zero defect" 当成信仰的半导体帝国掌舵人，公开表达对不完美的审美偏好——这是一个哲学级别的信号。

我的大胆预测：这不是闲话，这暗示 NVIDIA 内部已经在接受一个未来的事实——在 Blackwell 之后的尺度上，"完美良率"将不再是经济最优解。当芯片大到晶圆尺寸（wafer-scale, 像 Cerebras），当 chiplet 组合复杂到一定程度，容错架构会压过完美良率。Jensen 的 wabi-sabi 不是审美，是在为"冗余容错式计算"做心理铺垫。

换句话说：当他开始爱不完美，就是他准备卖不完美的时候。

📝 转录文本

偶遇与寒暄

Lex Fridman: Hey Jensen. Jensen Huang: Thanks. How's it going? Lex: Good to see you. Jensen: Welcome to Taiwan. Hey guys, do you know who this is? Crowd: Yes. Jensen: The great — Crowd: Yes. Love you. Lex: I love you, too. [laughter] Jensen: He's known worldwide as Lex, just like me, Jensen. Lex: You know you made it when you're just one — Jensen: You're just one name. Lex: Beyoncé. Jensen: Beyoncé. Lex: It's incredible. So much kindness. You're a rockstar. Jensen: Hey guys. Nice to see you. Nice to see you guys. Nice to see you guys.

"Jensenity" — 工程师的簇拥

Lex: Okay, this is legit. This is pretty insane. Jensenity. Jensen: Mike, do you know the famous Lex Fridman? Mike: Good to meet you. Jensen: Look at this guy. He went — he's just traveling through Asia. [laughter] Does everybody know the famous Lex Fridman? Fan: Stop it. Jensen, I love you. Jensen: Look at this. Look at this. [laughter]

100% 液冷与装配时间的革命

Jensen: No cables. No hoses. 100% liquid cooled. Lex: Yes. Jensen: Last generation Grace Blackwell was only 80% liquid cooled. Now it's 100% liquid cooled. From 2 hours to assemble, it's now 5 minutes. Things that are easy to build are also reliable. Lex: Officially in full production, right? Jensen: Yeah, full production now. Lex: Incredible, right? Jensen: Yeah, it's incredible. Lex: All this. Jensen: Everything.

CPU 的新经济学：从"核"到"token"

Lex: And the very CPU, you're full in on the CPU. I saw the 1.8x over x86. Jensen: x86 CPUs, the hyperscale CPUs, were designed to be rented. And so you want as many CPU cores as possible, because the economics of CPUs in the last generation was: what's the dollars per core.

In this new world, AI doesn't rent cores. AI generates tokens, and they sell tokens. And so your fundamental purpose is to go through that exchange, go through that loop as fast as you can, and generate tokens as fast as you can.

Lex: The more you buy, the more you make. You might be the best salesman in the world. [laughter] Jensen: It's easy. It's not a complicated thing. The technology is complicated, but the business model is — Lex: Amazing, amazing, amazing. [laughter]

签名与同游台湾

Jensen: All right, Lex. You got to sign here. "Lex was here, too." Lex: Yeah, all right. [laughter] Jensen: The great Lex Fridman. Lex: Yes. The love I'm getting from here is incredible. Jensen: No, he didn't happen to be here. He flew out to hang out. We're going to hang out for a couple days. I'm going to show him Taiwan. Fan: Awesome podcast. Very long ones. [laughter] Lex: Very, very long. Jensen: And you learn a lot, learn a lot. Lex: And learn a lot, and learn a lot. Thank you.

五层蛋糕与街头小吃

Jensen: AI is a five-layer cake. I think I'll have that one. Lex have — Lex: I think I have the — I have that the green one. Jensen: Did you enjoy some good food? Lex: Yeah. That street food is insane. [laughter] Jensen: This is good. This is a conference cake.

登台与"甲壳虫式"的玩笑

Host: Now, let's welcome Jensen and all our Computex executives on the stage. We're going to take one last group — Lex: Jensen Huang is like the Beatles in the '60s. Jensen: Except the Beatles actually had talent. Lex: Yeah, right. Well, I saw you dance on stage. It was all right. It was pretty good. [laughter] That wasn't quite John Travolta talent. [cheering] Remember that? Oh my goodness. Jensen: This is one of the best. I have so many happy memories of that.

SK Hynix 与 LPDDR4

Host: Ladies and gentlemen, welcome to SK Hynix — trillion-dollar company. No wonder supply so tight. Memory so big. You want to see something? Jensen: SK Hynix, legendary high bandwidth memory company. SK Hynix rep: We invented this — LPDDR4 memory into data centers. Twice the bandwidth, half the power. Jensen: And now, please make more. SK Hynix rep: Yeah, yeah. Please make more.

Wabi-sabi 时刻

Jensen: Oh, look at that. That's beautiful. You know, when I was young, I would think that that's not good. But now, I love wabi-sabi. You know, beautiful things — [don't need to] be perfect. Yeah. I love that. Lex: Imperfection is beauty. Jensen: Yeah, look at that. One of a kind.

老一代 GPU 的致敬

Lex: That's my favorite part — is all the different GPUs that people [bring], the old-school ones, all the old-school 1080, the Titan RTX — Jensen: 1080 generation. Titan. [cheering] You know, I've seen this on TV. [cheering] We're brothers. We're brothers. Lex: Yeah, we're brothers. Jensen: All right, we'll take it. Lex: Pretty good? Jensen: It's nice to have just a — I love this guy.

机械键盘与声控未来

Jensen: Oh, I love these keyboards. Lex, try this. Fan: Lex, mechanical? Lex: Oh god, they're the best. Jensen: Oh, nice. Lex: Look how delightful they feel. This — real joy. Jensen: I have bad news for you. Lex: Oh. Jensen: [In the] future, it's mostly going to be voice controlled. Lex: I think so, yeah. I think — better typing, do you? Jensen: Yeah, yeah. I have a hard time thinking when I'm just talking. Speed is not everything. Sometimes you have to pause and think. Look at that. Back to the '80s. Look at this. Thank you, brother.

收尾

Host: Ladies and gentlemen, Lex Fridman. Lex: Dàjiā hǎo.

## 一、Jensen 现象：硅片第一次拥有了"人格引力场"
视频里最震撼的不是技术，而是**一位芯片 CEO 被工程师围堵的场景**。这在半导体史上几乎没有先例——Intel 的 Grove、Krzanich、Gelsinger 走在街上没人认识；台积电张忠谋在西方几乎无面孔。而现在一个做 GPU 的黄仁勋，被叫做"Beatles"。
这背后藏着一个被忽略的转折：**AI 让硅第一次"可见"。** 过去三十年，芯片是一个"消失的产业"——它越成功，越不可见（埋在服务器里、嵌在手机里）。而生成式 AI 让每一次对话都能被追溯到"是哪块芯片在算"，于是硬件突然有了叙事权。黄仁勋不是靠营销成为明星的，他是**第一个"被 token 抬起来"的硬件家**。
跨领域连接：这其实复刻了 19 世纪末**爱迪生-特斯拉时代**的工程师崇拜——那也是基础设施（电）从不可见转向可见的时刻。每当底层能源被重新定义，底层能源的"面孔"就会被神化。你现在看到的 Jensenity，是**算力即电力**这个事实的社会化外显。

item.title: [Odds on Open] Hedge Fund Manager Joseph Walsh: Always Play Weaker Players
item.dc:creator: Odds on Open
item.content:encoded:
💡 创造性洞见

一、最意外的观察：他其实在"反向使用"扑克——不是赢得牌局，而是选择不去的牌桌

大多数人读到"扑克手优势"会立刻想到：读心、心理战、虚张声势、GTO 策略。但 Walsh 几乎完全不谈这些。他承认自己"甚至没进过前百分位"，却靠扑克赚到钱——靠的是选桌而不是打牌。

这里藏着一个被整个投资行业系统性忽视的真相：绝大多数"选股方法论"书籍都在教你如何打牌，但顶级 Alpha 来自于拒绝坐上某些牌桌。 他对冲基金的核心框架不是"我能比谁更聪明"，而是"在哪个时间尺度上、哪个流动性区间里，聪明人已经退场了？" 他明确说：3-6 个月视角的欧洲工业股——那是多策略平台的屠宰场，不去；流动性 1000-3000 万美元/日的名字——他们因杠杆约束进不来，所以我去。

这是一种负向定义的 edge：不是"我强在哪"，而是"对手弱在哪、或根本不来"。换个说法——他的 Alpha 不是技能溢价，而是结构性缺席套利。

二、跨领域连接：Walsh 的"时间尺度套利"与生态学的"生态位分化"是同一个数学结构

生物学里有个 Gause 竞争排斥原理：两个物种若占据完全相同的生态位，必有一个灭绝。于是进化的真正故事不是"更强"，而是生态位分化——猫头鹰夜间捕食、鹰白天捕食，同一片森林两种生物共存。

Walsh 本能地做了同样的事。多策略平台在 1-6 个月时间尺度 × 10M+ 流动性 × 低 beta 约束的生态位里是顶级掠食者。他没有正面硬刚，而是迁移到了另一个生态位：12+ 个月视角 × 小流动性池 × 可承受集中度。这不是"我更擅长投资"，而是"我吃不同的食物"。

更有意思的推论：随着多策略平台 AUM 持续膨胀，它们的生态位反而在收窄——杠杆越高，可投品种越受流动性限制。Walsh 的生态位因此在被动扩大。这解释了一个反直觉现象：对冲基金行业越拥挤，专注"非主流时间尺度"的小基金 edge 越大，而不是越小。市场效率不是均匀上升的，它是在特定生态位里上升、在其他生态位里下降。

三、最被低估的那句话："早期 Alpha 是最好的 Alpha"——它暗示了一个心理学的残酷真相

他轻描淡写地说："从 100 涨到 500 和从 500 涨到 1000 都是 100% 收益，但在电子表格上看不出前者比后者好得多。"

这不是技术分析话术。这是在说：人类的大脑系统性低估了"确定性的隐藏成本"。 后期上涨看起来"更安全"是因为叙事更清晰、共识更强——但清晰的叙事恰恰是风险溢价消失的标志。你以 500 买入 Palantir 比以 100 买入感觉更安全，但按风险调整后收益看，感觉越安全的交易，边际 Alpha 越低。

跨领域连接——这正是认知科学里的"解释深度错觉"（Illusion of Explanatory Depth）：一件事被反复解释，大脑把"熟悉"误认成"理解"，把"理解"误认成"低风险"。市场把这种错觉定价化了：当一个故事被反复讲述、被 CNBC 嘉宾口若悬河地解释，PE 扩张就是在为这种集体错觉付费。

所以 Walsh 的真正方法论不是"买早"，而是"卖早"。 他承认几乎每次都卖得太早。但这不是缺陷——这是他的核心风控：在市场把你的洞见"叙事化"之前离场。因为一旦故事被广泛接受，你的 Alpha 就从"信息差"变成了"情绪差"——而情绪差是他明确说不想和多策略平台/散户竞争的那个战场。

一个让人汗毛直立的推论：今天你最有信心的那只 AI 股票，可能正是你 Alpha 最低的那只。 不是因为它基本面变差了，而是因为你对它的"确信感"本身，就是集体叙事成熟的信号。

📝 转录文本

Hedge Fund Manager Joseph Walsh: Always Play Weaker Players

开场

Ethan: Your returns are great. Sortino over two, 60% annualized.

What are the advantages associated with being a great poker player for investing? Do you like to buy on the way up or buy on the way down? The expected value of buying a stock at 100 on a certain day and 100 on a different day, they're not the same.

What great returns look like are high compounding with no blow ups. That's the holy grail.

Joe, thank you so much for coming on the pod.

Joe: Ethan, thank you for having me and congrats on the success and growth of your show.

一、扑克手的优势：缺失信息博弈与风险管理

Ethan: What are the advantages associated with being a great poker player for investing?

Joe: I think so i'm not an active poker player nowadays but i take a lot from my time as a younger man uh playing the game and i think you know there's a particularly on the trading side you know pure investing and you know maybe there are fewer parallels but in the trading side of the business there are several transferable skill sets where great poker players naturally would have some advantage at also being good at trading.

So one of those would be that they're effectively both games of missing information. So, you know, in poker, you have 52 cards, you have certain variables that are constrained. In the game of No Limit Hold'em, you would be dealt two cards. So you now know there are 50 remaining cards in the deck. You have card removal effects as cards are dealt on the board. You know, there's more card removal effects. You know, every single one of these pieces of information affects the odds of certain hands being made. And also, there's so many variables in that game, but it basically transcends really well across the arena of trading.

风险管理：赢家还要避免成为输家

I think great poker players ultimately are very good risk managers. There are people who are very winning poker players, but they never make it to the top of that arena because their risk management isn't good enough and they're able to generate huge wins, but they're not able to preserve capital as a great hedge fund manager needs to preserve capital as they're stalking the next asymmetric investment in their portfolio.

So it's not enough to be a winner. You also have to avoid being a loser effectively and great poker players who have generated long, durable careers, if you could call playing poker a career, which, you know, for the very best, they've managed to carve that out for themselves, they all have that very disciplined bankroll management.

市场效率与学习的赛跑

They study very hard, which the greatest investors and greatest traders do because they understand that market efficiency as a function of time goes up. I've seen that in my time in markets for the last 14 years. When I came in, stocks were often in the markets I was investing and trading in, they were way wrong. Those gaps close over time, but as you get better, your ability to monetize those situations and spot them earlier increases. So you basically have to increase your edge faster than the market becomes efficient for your edge to grow.

Game Selection：始终对阵更弱的玩家

And yeah, aside from studying to improve and managing risk, capital, or in a poker vernacular, your bankroll well, great poker players are usually also very good at game selection. So, be making sure that, you know, if you're risking money against other players or in a trading situation, you know, it might be market making at a huge firm versus market making at another huge firm. You always, the basic premise is you always want to make sure you're up against weaker players.

So myself, I wouldn't say I was the world's gift to poker, far from it. I'm not even in the top percentiles or whatever. I was not a great player, but I had great results. And that was mainly because at least within the areas of bankroll management, and being able to select good games and things like that, I did a good enough job, not a world-class job, but I did a good enough job that I was able to generate really good returns.

And yeah, I mean, that was a long time ago, but I carry a lot of those lessons and particularly the mathematics and statistics of, you know, expected value, variance, these dominate my thinking in terms of how I appraise any random variable, how I look at the world. It's quite probabilistic. So hopefully that gives you a general framework on some of the key skills and how it's so transferable to the markets.

二、投资中的 Game Selection：避开最聪明的对手

Ethan: On game selection and how great poker players are able to pick good games, I'd love to hear about how that weaves into your process.

Joe: Yeah, thanks for the kind words. Yeah, I could have been taking a huge amount of risk, but I guess the Sortino statistic you calculated covers that. But yeah, the answer to how I think about, I guess, game selection to borrow that is you want to be in stocks, in sectors and in markets where you basically are in anti-competitive situations where different pools of capital have different agendas. You're not against the most talented investors.

被动投资与多策略平台如何重塑市场结构

There are lots of market forces and market structure that's probably good to visit at this moment in terms of understanding what drives pricing and inefficiency. So there's been huge growth in passive investing. There's been huge growth in AUM inside of multi-strategy hedge funds.

And passive investing is largely a price indiscriminate buyer or seller of an asset. where it's payroll linked and employment linked at the end of the month, someone gets their check and a certain portion of it via a pension deduction or otherwise goes into the BlackRock ETF that the pension fund manager has decided upon. I'm oversimplifying, but you get the point. There's no discerning of which stock is the best stock. It's just whatever's in that ETF is getting bought at that moment, regardless of value.

So I think most people understand that and the growth of that from being 6% of flows to over like half of flows is really material in terms of, I guess, how stocks get priced because effectively just by definition, you do get a misallocation of capital because where ETFs are market cat weighted, the big receive more and you get it's basically a momentum trade. Things that have gone up, get more inflows, things that have gone down, get less. And so you get a perpetuation of that.

Where you have an increasing share of AUM being run in equity books at up to eight times GMV, in fixed income books, you know, greater than 10 times GMV, sometimes up to 15 times. And this is all available by PB data and industry surveys. And then allocators are allocating into these platforms under SMAs, using leverage from their prime broker accounts, they're ultimately volatility targeting and they're very good. They're some of the best firms in the world at delivering like volatility targeted returns. So they're good at delivering cash plus equity returns with a desirable sharp, whether that be like 1.5 net to the client after fees. But, you know, internally they gross at a higher sharp than that. But the product is volatility targeting, it's not profit maximizing. So they're always running on a centralized risk limit with stops, factor constrained, beta constrained.

时间尺度与赛道选择

And so tying all of these factors back into game selection and picking stocks, I think the first thing I think about is time horizon. I don't want to be looking at a security and valuing it on a three to six month timeframe where I'm competing against another very well resourced, motivated man or woman who is working inside of one of these firms that has got way better corporate access, has got way better access to short term information, proprietary data sets.

And whilst a ton of this has been democratized, particularly in this current AI moment, and so the playing field is being leveled and it's actually a wonderful time to be a smaller investor or be running a smaller fund, the fact is, is you've got to pick your time horizons to be avoiding very good players, you've got to pick your sectors where all of the pods who used to do that have been shut down and all of the investors have given up. And you typically get that in cyclical sectors, but whatever it looks like, the game selection aspect is running away from competition. And that's where greater inefficiency by definition lives.

And there are huge pockets of that in the equity market today. So time horizon is a big one. If you think you're going to have a huge edge trading European industrials on a three month timeframe, trying to have a better view on earnings and the delta between market value and earnings, I would politely disagree with most people that they wouldn't have an edge there. But for ourselves, we have huge edge in timeframes that are greater than 12 months in different sectors and different markets where it's just not as competitive.

And that can be for reasons of it's not worth these people's time when they're running 100 billion of capital levered multiple times to muck around in names that have got liquidity of 10, 20, $30 million a day. It's just the liquidity constraint might be unattractive for them, but the capacity with which I could run money is very attractive to single digit billions and still have a huge edge and still remain very liquid.

So hopefully that gives you a sense of some of the things that drive decision making when it comes to thinking about where to look and where great returns might lie and the time horizon over which they could be extracted.

广告插播：Onyx Capital Group / Flux

Alds on Open is sponsored by Onyx Capital Group, the top market maker in oil derivatives. They just released the fourth version of the terminal, Flux, and there are two things in it worth knowing if you have oil exposure.

First, it streams live fair value on 800 oil curves, including the ones that are hard to mark. Second, it carries their own positioning data, so you can see how the market is positioned long and short and at what price they got in.

You can find it at Flux.live and the link is in the description.

三、负 Gamma 事件与去杠杆窗口：从 SVB 到 Liberation Day

Ethan: On the pods, we know each other through a very talented PM at one of the pod shops. And these guys are very intelligent. You do not want to compete with them. What sort of markets today do you operate in that you feel there is good amount of edge in?

Joe: Well, as a generalist, I don't typically box myself in. You have to have breadth in terms of the amount of sectors you have good opinions on, understand the companies within. There's no real shortcut there. I've been doing this for 14 years and it just takes time. It takes a tire work. It's reading hundreds of annual reports. It's listening to manager interviews. It's going to conferences, meeting these people, going on site visits, visiting these companies, visiting these sites. It just takes time.

多策略平台造成的流动性级联

And yeah, in terms of, I guess, avoiding them is maybe too strong. It's more understanding where they are and where the mechanism they work within can create moments of opportunity. So I think it's kind of an increasing feature of today's market structure that has risen with their growth that you see more and more of these negative gamma events in the equity market which results from crowdedness, leverage, degracing to tight risk mandates.

You know, the liquidity cycle in the short term bottomed in the fourth quarter of 2022. There were some unbelievable opportunities we could talk about that, you know, took advantage of then. But very quickly after that, in March of 2023, there was a mini banking crisis with Silicon Valley Bank, and there was very, very rapid degracing that took place. And there were equities that frankly just dislocated meaningfully from where they should have because you had this liquidation effect. And it was a rapid V-shaped dip. And once the degracing had finished, everyone had puked out what they needed to puke out, the market ripped straight back. And that was obviously matched with some kind of policy response within the banking system because Silicon Valley wasn't the only one to get shut down there at Silvergate.

But just fast forwarding 5th of August the next year in 2024, there was a Yen Carry blowout. And again, you know, that was a very, very short, sharp drawdown where risk just got puked. And, you know, where there's a lot of concentration, a lot of crowdedness, and there's a huge amount of assets running on leverage in certain situations, you just get one guy's stop is selling causes and assets and fall further, hits the next stop and their liquidation cascades.

Liberation Day：史上最大情绪恐慌之一

And so then, you know, the one that's quite vivid in people's minds was obviously, you know, the second week of April 2025, Liberation Day. And that was a very interesting setup because the driver of that was entirely within the US administration's control. Basically, they were levying tariffs and people didn't like it. But to the extent things were getting really drastic, you know, they were always in a position to walk that back.

But in the depths of that pullback where the S&P was clearing at 4,800 points, you had financial conditions in the US as measured by some of the index at levels lower than the 2011 Eurozone crisis. The only reading that was lower on those indexes was the depths of September 2008. You could read portfolio manager surveys that were highlighting the sentiment in the market was worse than 2008, which was astonishing to me at the time, but it was giving me a ton of, I guess, confidence that we were approaching a bottom, particularly when you looked at the drivers of that situation.

And then, yeah, you were just ultimately as a stock picker, you were going into your businesses and particularly the most robust franchises where on a per share basis, some of these businesses are so strong that they're not very cyclical. They're very defensive. They're very high margin. They're high quality businesses. They generate very high free cash flow margins over sales. And in that particular instance, for example, where you might have a tariff impact in your business.

And so if you've got a ton of pricing power and there's one stock in particular I'm thinking about right now, while I'm talking about this on their earnings call, they just said, if they put these tariffs through, our customers love us, that we're just going to pass it straight through. And they literally just wiped their brow and carried on. And the stock exploded like a rocket out of it, like the market did.

不是在躲，而是在"理解"多策略平台

But it's not that you're avoiding like multi-stratus, so to speak. You're kind of aware of them. You're not trying to play in the same realm, you're not trying to do what they do because you're just not going to be as good as they are. You know, you're more of an investor who does a ton of fundamental work, but you understand that this participant can have a disproportionate impact on price in certain moments in the market.

And there are other aspects like the passive aspect and the proliferation of leverage products, the participation of retail, you know, there's tax loss harvesting products. There are a ton of factors now in today's market structure where as a fundamental analyst trying to value a business, the stock can deviate far further away from where the business is worth than the you would think possible in the short term.

But to the extent you understand the market structure and why it's happening, that's a huge opportunity. And so in terms of selecting your game and selecting your moments to size up, and where you've got multiple layers of margin of safety on your thesis because positioning's flushed out, valuation's flushed out, market's flushed out. You know, you can get these moments where I personally don't run much, if any, portfolio leverage, but I preserve my balance sheet very deliberately for those moments where the volatility is erupting and you can take advantage of the volatility and not be taken advantage of by it. Because the last thing you want to be is the last person to get spot out and you print the low, and the train leaves the station without you, that's a disaster and that's quite detrimental to your compounding over time.

四、仓位管理：常态期保守，波动期果断加码

Ethan: How much typically do you deploy during normal periods? And then how much do you leave on the side to plough into those moments where you have extremely high conviction? Do you lever up?

Joe: Yeah, it's a very, very good question. And the truth is it's changed over time because the markets have changed over time. So I think I'm happy to go into how I think about it today, but I almost am obliged to give you the caveat that my thinking on this subject will evolve as markets evolve. And so I can almost promise you I'll think about this differently in three to five years time as markets evolve and my process hopefully improves as I keep working on this.

常态下的做法

Yeah, how I think about it in times of normalcy is, as I said, you know, I'm really filtering for robustness in, you know, on the long side versus the short side. I mean, I'll talk about longs to start. But yeah, in longs, you want, you know, robust operating structures, you want robust capital structures, you want robust ownership structures.

Sizing for me is done on a security by security basis in a market by market basis. I would love to sit here and I love Ed Thorpe, great mathematician, great returns he generated and just be able to sit here, Ethan, and say, I just do Kelly criterion and that's how I size and it's just a formula that I try to leverage fundamentals to understand where evaluation could get to where there's a huge amount of skewness asymmetry in the forward-looking returns and so, you know, it's really expected value over variance.

In times of normalcy, I'm not running much portfolio leverage. And from a top-down level, that determines, okay, I've got this much gross, I'm running, I'm keeping balance sheet optionality on the side. And within that, along in the short book could be, you know, a big position might be X and a small position might be a third of X.

波动期的加码艺术

But really, the kind of the craft, I would call it, is when you do get dislocations and things start getting very volatile, knowing where you're adding and knowing where you're not and where you're cutting is really, really important. And that really is planned way ahead of time by doing fundamental, deep fundamental work on knowing the business intimately, the industry structure within which it's operating, the regulatory structure under which it operates. These are all very important inputs on top of market structure, which is typically driving that volatility in a given moment that we've already covered.

And so what it frankly comes down to without boring you with huge amounts of detail is where you get multiple layers of margin of safety, I'm going to start exponentially increasing my bet size. And so there's a very good trader who deserves a shout out, who's phenomenally generous with his knowledge called Lance Breistein. And he articulates this really well in terms of trading with skewness and his setups of like a C, a B and an A trade. And that's a very good way to think about it. And it's not too dissimilar from how I trade myself.

Where the margin of safety is greatest, or if you think in equity risk premium terms, where returns are greatest, risk is lowest, that's where you want to be deploying the most amounts of capital relative to your risk framework. And that's how I've done it. And that's how I've generated good returns with pretty good risk metrics.

Conviction 无法借用

It's patience and it's composure. And in those moments, not panicking, but you can't borrow conviction. You can't shortcut it. You have to earn it through hundreds of hours of research. You have to answer all those tough questions of what if this happens? What if that happens? What if a competitor does this?

And when you've turned over every stone and you know most of the answers to a level where you've exhausted it and you're very comfortable with the drivers, as long as those drivers are in place, and you take a situation where a market is up here and market value is this, and then something happens and market value is down 25%, as long as the quality and the depth of your work supports the fact that intrinsic value, which may have been on a base of 100, 150, and the equity would now be trading at 70. If a company has missed earnings and something terrible has happened, it's not reasonable for you to sit there and continue to argue that intrinsic value is 150. That might be the case, but it's probably not because something's going wrong in that business and the market's reacting accordingly.

But there are plenty of situations where intrinsic value is completely unaffected, something's happening and market value is going down. And there are those rare situations where actually intrinsic value is rising as market value is declining. And those are the real diamond setups where you can really size up.

But having the confidence in your assessments and your forecasts, it goes down to doing huge amounts of work, you know, building the models, reading the annual reports, meeting the companies, meeting the competitors. I wish there were an easy way to have that conviction, but it just takes so much studying and continually reading the filings and carrying on.

And again, it goes into the depth of work in, you know, a basic example would be if you have a stock with a market cap of 100 and it, you know, it trades at two times sales. But, you know, it's not enough to do that on an individual stock basis. You know, frankly, I think where I generate a lot of edge is on industry structure. So understanding where a dollar flows in to a value chain and how each part of the value chain takes a different amount of the profit pool and understanding from inception to finish where the profit pool actually accumulates, either on a gross profit or net profit basis, and then where returns on capital over that profit are exceptional or much better than sector average, and then understanding how industry structure has changed over time.

So if it's a dynamically changing industry like semiconductors or tech, that's a form of fragility because today's frontier technology can reach obsolescence when the next generation comes out. But if you're analyzing the luxury sector and you're dealing with a handful of brands that have been around for over a century, when you're looking at a company like Hermes or Louis Vuitton or even entities that are private just for comparisons like Chanel, you know, the industry structure doesn't change nearly as much there. It's quite static. It's not dynamic.

And so where industry structure becomes predictable, profit pools of certain entities become very predictable. The confidence interval around your forecast compresses. And so your confidence in that forecast rises, and the probability of you being way wrong declines and the variance of that return being achieved comes down.

So sizing for me and it's borrowing that expected value framework that we touched on at the start, you know, it's really expected value over the volatility of that expected value being achieved. But it's all driven by fundamental research. And, you know, on entries and exits, I use technical analysis. It's extremely helpful in terms of when things are breaking out, when things are breaking down, knowing when to be hitting the accelerator, when to be hitting the brake, but it's all augmenting that fundamental work and knowing what things are worth because you can't really have a view on this is a very good long or this is a very good short without having a great sense of what it's worth to start.
