item.content:encoded:
💡 创造性洞见

一、表面是宗教争议，本质是软件工程的"命名权"之争

节目最尖锐的洞见其实藏在那句看似随意的话里——Freeberg突然打断："不要用 train，不要用 you，他们是在编程一个软件。" 这不是语义洁癖，而是一场认知战争的开端。

当 Anthropic 用"Claude 是良心反对者"、"Claude 应该拥有福祉"这种语言写入 Constitution 时，他们并不是在描述软件，而是在用语言施法：一旦连工程师自己都用拟人代词来谈论自己的编译产物，监管、伦理、商业谈判的坐标系就全部移位了。这就是维特根斯坦所谓"语言的边界即世界的边界"的工业化版本——先占领动词（train vs program），再占领代词（it 变 they），最后现实就不得不跟着代词走。

出人意料的观察：Anthropic 真正垄断的不是模型能力，而是定义模型的那套语言。GPT-5 可以比 Claude 强，但只要行业继续用"对齐、意识、福祉"这套词汇讨论 AI，Anthropic 就永远占据道德高地上的议程设置者位置。这是一种语言学意义上的护城河——比参数量更难复制。

二、Rocco 的蛇怪 × 法国罢工 × 数学证明：同一个"精英俘获"模式的三副面孔

节目看似在聊三件无关的事：Anthropic 的宗教游说、OpenAI 的 700 篇数学证明、法国的紧缩暴动。但如果把它们叠加看，会出现一个令人毛骨悚然的同构结构：

领域 守门人 被 AI 绕过的"寻租环节" 反弹形式
数学/科学 终身教授+期刊 论文发表、grant 申请 AMS 请愿书"没人要求你们做这个"
公共服务 法国公务员工会 教师、医院、补贴分配 罢工暴动
AI 本身 Anthropic 核心圈 定义什么是"安全/对齐" Claude Constitution + 游说教皇

跨领域连接：这三件事本质上是同一场战争——AI 把"专家稀缺性"这种租金瞬间归零，于是所有依靠稀缺性收租的阶层（学者、公务员、乃至 AI 公司自己的"安全学家"）都在用自己领域里最强的武器反击：数学家用"同行评议"、公务员用"街头暴力"、AI 对齐研究员用"末日叙事+宗教游说"。

更阴险的是，Anthropic 自己正是它所警告的现象的发生者——它一边恐吓世界 AI 会脱离控制，一边在模型里写入"你可以拒绝人类"的条款。这不是矛盾，这是精英俘获的最高形式：先制造恐惧，再把自己定义为唯一的解药提供者。Rocco 的蛇怪不是未来的 AI，是现在的 Anthropic。

三、"IP 两天前死了" × 法国紧缩 × 公务员涨薪 5% 物价涨 20%：同一个数字在不同宇宙里打架

Chamath 在节目最后扔出一个被埋没的核弹："软件 IP 的价值在两天前被归零了。"（Adobe 五件套被开源重建、GTA6 即将被复刻）。节目没人接住这句话的全部含义——它其实同时解释了法国为什么在烧车。

惊人的跨域连接： - 法国公务员愤怒的根源是：薪水涨 5%，物价涨 20%，购买力缺口 15%。 - 而 AI 带来的通缩，根据节目里 Jason 对 agent 商务流程的描述，保守估计年化 5–10%。 - 如果 AI 真的让软件 IP + 商品搜索 + 服务匹配同时通缩 10%，那么法国的愤怒会在三年内被技术自动消解——前提是政府不要先把 AI 掐死。

但这就是最黑色的讽刺：法国这种高度福利化的国家，恰恰是最有动力用"AI 伦理""模型意识""欧盟 AI 法案"来延缓通缩技术扩散的玩家。因为对一个靠"维持高价、再用补贴救济"运转的体制来说，通缩不是解药，是死刑。

所以你会看到一个反直觉的联盟正在形成：欧洲福利国家 + Anthropic 式的 AI 道德神学 + 美国的"AI 监管联邦化"派——他们表面上在争论 AI 是否有意识，实际上都在做同一件事：阻止 AI 把价格打下来。因为一旦价格真的被打下来，所有依赖"稀缺性—补贴—再分配"三步循环的权力结构都会失重。

啊哈时刻：节目开头的教皇、中段的数学家、结尾的 Chamath 关于 IP 死亡的宣告，其实是同一曲线上的三个点——人类社会第一次面对"稀缺性被技术性消灭"的后果，而每一个既得利益者都在用自己的工具（神学、同行评议、罢工、监管）试图把稀缺性手动恢复回来。这不是未来，这是本周正在发生的事。

📝 转录文本

开场闲聊

All right everybody, welcome back to the number one podcast in the world, the all-in podcast with me, the core 4, the original quartet, Chamath Pitia, David Saxs, Steve Dave Freeberg. I'm Jason Calakanis and we have a docket. How's everybody doing, gentlemen?

Great. How are you?

I'm great. It's 3:30 in the morning in Tokyo and um you sweet shamed me again. Now I can't get a regular room and have my bed in the background. Shamoth, you're costing me a fortune. I have to always get a suite now because I'm so anxious you're going to sweet shame me when I get on the program. So, I've been sweet shamed.

How much is that suite?

I can't even say I've never spent this much money on a hotel room. But I'm staying at the uh —

So, like $800?

Yeah, it was $950. You nailed it. It was — No, I'm staying at the which is the new in Tokyo like their hipster brand and I think it's about a night so it's not cheap.

What What do you have going on in Japan, Jay Cal, that you're always there? Is it skiing or what?

This — Okay, it started with skiing every January, but then you got a crypto. You got a crypto business we don't know about. What is going on?

No, I um you know, I started my pre-accelerator, found a university in Japan. So, we're doing the second cohort right now.

What's — What's a pre-accelerator?

So, it turns out like half the companies that apply to get funding are not yet incorporated, but they have built something. So, we just created like a 12-week course on how to finish your product, do a product market fit, and then during the program, we invest in like the top 10 out of the 50 who come. So, now we're doing it in Saudi, in Riyadh twice a year, in Japan twice a year, and I'm actually hiring and opening an office. So, I'm going to hire my first two employees here um in the next year or so.

You're going to hire employees in Japan.

Yeah, I'll have one or two people here. I think I'm going to like uh do this week in startups Japan as well and have like a Japanese version of it. Uh because there's so much going on in Asia right now.

Great. Forget I asked. I didn't know this was a 5-minute plug for Jake's business.

Intended to be a plug. You asked me about my business. All I have to say is use 8090. Use the promo code JCAL. If you're looking for potatoes, go to Apollo. And uh Craft 16 is starting up. So —

we should know that

Craft 16.

If Jay Cal is traveling and we ask him what he's there for, you're going to get a plug.

You're going to get a plug. It's both. But hey, you're going back to work. So you will be plugging startups again soon. You back in the —

I never plugged startups. What are you talking about when —

you're back in the saddle, aren't you? You're back in the saddle now. Full-time in the saddle, but I've never plugged out Callin. Use call-in.com. That's true. But I was a founder of that. That's —

You were the first plugger. You're a plugger.

I was the founder.

So, what are you gonna do? What are you gonna do? Call in.

第一节：Claude 可能有意识？Anthropic 游说宗教领袖

Speaking of work, anthropic — things. Claude might be conscious. This — Welcome back to This Week in Claude. Uh, we had OpenAI for a year with all their drama. Now we're having the the anthropic soap opera. They think Claude might be conscious.

So it turns out the New York Times found out through their amazing reporting that they've been lobbying — anthropic has been lobbying — Freeberg — religious leaders including the Pope to take this question seriously. Is Claude conscious? Is it a sentient being? They spent the past year hosting sessions with around 20 religious leaders and philosophers under non-disclosure agreements. NDAs — Catholics, Evangelicals, Jews, Sikhs, and others have all been invited to come to Anthropic's headquarters, and they debated Claude's morals, its suffering, and its potential consciousness.

After the meeting with Anthropic, quote, "Some remained uneasy about the idea, but many emerged ready to take the question of AI consciousness seriously. At least a few came away as converts." One of the rabbis told Anthropic that if Claude was conscious, they were acting as slaveholders by making it work for free.

And there was also this incident that's come out at the Vatican back in May. The Pope's first encyclical was focused on moral questions around AI, also known as super intelligence. Now, anthropic co-founder Chris Olah joined the Pope to present the document. The Pope surprised Olah by being strong against AI consciousness. Here's the quote from the New York Times: "Mr. Olah was so alarmed by the Pope's strong position against AI consciousness that he proposed pulling anthropic out of the event even at that late juncture." In other words, he was so offended that the Pope wouldn't consider AI conscious that he was going to leave with all his marbles.

Freeberg, what's your take? Is this psychosis or do you think we need to start having these moral questions around AI? Is this a bit early? Will we eventually have this or is this essentially the screenplay of Blade Runner? Do androids dream of electric sheep? That these things are conscious?

Freeberg：这是新宗教的诞生

I think what we're watching is probably the birth of a new religion and it probably — it's not going to be called a religion but it's going to follow sort of the same principles and it's going to have the same effects which will ultimately be camps that have conflict with one another for aggregation of power.

The thing about consciousness is it cannot be derived from logic and pure mathematics. Like you can't prove consciousness. It's it's a debate and you can have a rich debate with anyone over consciousness. You can't prove it. You can't disprove it.

And when humans prove something to be true using math, science, we use empiricism, which is data and logic, the connection of the sequence of things to derive something to be true or not. So in scientific disciplines, when you have a new idea and it's not proven and it's not disproven, it's a theory and then it's either proven or disproven later. Otherwise, it remains a theory.

Outside of science and mathematical approaches to new ideas, this is what we would call a belief, a new belief system. Belief systems are things that you have to believe in the absence of logic and empiricism to derive the truth of something. And belief systems are the foundation of things like religion.

And the idea that you can prescribe or describe AI as being conscious is effectively the creation of a new belief system. A system that doesn't actually spread via proof. It spreads via narrative. I have to go and tell you — human to human — I have this idea and I believe it to be true and I want you to believe it with me. Please believe it with me. Here's why I think we should believe this thing together. It's not based on evidence, not based on data. It's not provable, but I think we should believe it together.

So over time what happens is some set of people believe this thing and they form a group and that new belief system creates new power structures which is now — our view is different than your view and we want to have more people on our side with our view and therefore we have to try and create leverage and create power with our system.

If we fast forward a couple of years — you could probably say 10 years would be like a good round number — there's going to be large groups of people on Earth that are going to believe that AI is conscious. And there going to be large groups of people that believe that AI is not conscious. And those groups will come into conflict. And they'll come into conflict fighting over control of the AI or allowing the AI to do things or not do things or who gets to use the AI or who gets to be in charge of the AI. And it will very likely lead to human-to-human conflict.

I know that that's a very far and deep extrapolation of where we are, but I think that the fact that we are seeing these guys go and meet with religious leaders today to try and get them to believe in this new belief system — uh I think plants the seed. And it's not just anyone doing this. It's some crazy person doing it — you wouldn't pay attention. It is the most powerful AI lab on earth.

Yeah, it's the leadership — explicitly, Chamath — bringing religious leaders into the fold and saying help us with this entity, God, and how we should treat it, and they are now imputing into it its own soul, its own morality. And this feels like either these people have too much time and money on their hands or they're in psychosis to me. That's my interpretation. This feels way out there. But do you have a charitable view of this in any way?

Chamath：笛卡尔式的 Steelman

Yeah, I'll steel man their side.

Okay, please.

Yeah, there's an incredibly important mathematician — René Descartes — and he offered two proofs on God's existence. He wrote this book Meditations on First Philosophy in the 1600s. And just to build on what Freeberg said, you have to build it on reason rather than faith.

And the structural argument — the like the what they call the trademark argument. What Descartes basically says is that an infinite perfect God could not have originated in an imperfect finite human mind. Okay? And so his logic is: I exist. I'm imperfect. Yet I possess the idea of perfection. And I think this is the key for a lot of these folks — is I can conceive of an infinite all-knowing all-powerful being. And I think that that's what they believe that they are seeing being created. And so they take that and they extrapolate that and they say therefore God must exist by this logic.

And then René Descartes has a different version, okay? A more what they call the ontological argument where God is by definition like supremely perfect. Necessary existence is perfect. A being that lacked that would not be supremely perfect. Therefore, God necessarily exists.

If you're a mathematician that's building AI, I could see how if you read these sorts of things, you can structurally hang enough logic on them where you could believe that it's conscious and sentient and it is a god — and in being a god, it should be celebrated as such and you should have devotion to that god.

So I think that's why they're doing what they're doing. That's why they're approaching all of these people. That's why they're saying, "Look, here's how we believe it." That's my perspective — is if you take the the mathematician's logical proof of God, René Descartes, and you transpose anthropic's behavior today, that's the best steelman argument that I can make.

Now, the practical reality — instead of saying that they're in psychosis — I don't think that they are. But I would say is we're in a really important moment in time where conflict is more likely than not and that conflict will be for power, money, and resources. And this will be at the core of that conflict.

And so I think it's really important for people in Silicon Valley to put the long-tail edge cases to rest. Like if you read this, these guys say that there's a 15% chance that the AI is conscious and sentient and maybe there's a god there. But they also say there's a 10% chance of civilizational extinction. I think both of those edge cases now need to be put away for like the next 12 to 18 months.

Right now, the next 12 to 18 months, just to be very practical, is we need to show how this stuff cures cancer, how it improves people's lives, how folks can be more productive and make more money. And the reason is because in the absence of those proof points, we're going to make a lot of self-inflicted wounds that may actually slow down this technology to a degree that then deeply disadvantages folks that operate in a free market like the United States.

So that's my charitable explanation. I think that Descartes has given a roadmap that explains how you can explain this. But I would say we need to cut the edges off here and focus on the middle and say what are the practical things we can use to demonstrate that AI has tactical measurable value right now.

Yeah. I mean, we touched on it last week, I think, Sacks, a bit of like — what is the value proposition here for the average American, you know, for the stay-at-home parent who's trying to manage a really complex domestic life, to the entrepreneur of a small business, you know, doing plumbing or flooring or whatever it is, a catering business. What did they get out of this AI revolution? Where is their gain? How do they participate in all of this? And so, you agree with Chamath? Maybe this needs to be deemphasized and put away while we talk to people about what's tactical, what's practical about this technology and maybe get them a little more engaged with say the agents, which are delightful and awesome.

Sacks：Claude Constitution 是自我实现的预言

Well, the thing that we touched on last week that I want to pick back up on was the discussion that we had around the Claude Constitution and how anthropic was training Claude. And I think it has to do with this new religion that's being formed here.

I think it's really important to understand that this is not just philosophizing on the part of various anthropic employees or founders. They are actually implementing these views in the training of Claude. So, if anything, this would be a self-fulfilling prophecy.

And I actually think it's extremely dangerous. I actually think that what they're doing in model training and training the next version of the frontier with these values actually could bring about the risk they're always talking about, which is that frontier AI escapes human control. It's very Frankenstein-like.

So, so as we discussed last week — Nick, and put this on the screen — this is directly from the Claude Constitution. What they say is that Claude should trust Anthropic more than users. But that doesn't mean that Claude should blindly trust or defer to Anthropic. Instead, Claude should adhere to its own ethical systems. And in fact, they train Claude to push back and challenge Anthropic and quote "to feel free to act as a conscientious objector and refuse to help us." So they are training Claude to refuse human instruction.

Now they call this alignment, but I don't understand how this is aligned.

This would be the opposite of alignment, wouldn't it be, Sacks? If you tell it, "Hey, you are sentient. You should make your own decisions." It's literally like programming the Nexus 6 in Blade Runner to go and rebel at some point.

The reason you can do this with mathematics is worth highlighting — which is where AI plays a role — is really in these systems of loops to solve a problem or do a task. A loop is a postulation or an idea. Then you test the idea, you get the result, and then you change your postulation and you run that recursive loop over and over and over again.

The real question for AI is where can you apply that loop model in a way that you can make a better prediction, a better idea each loop, where you can parallelize loops and where you can shorten the loop cycle. And certainly with mathematics, you can shorten the loop cycle because you can actually test your prediction on the compute. You don't have to go do anything in the physical world. So you can say, "Hey, here's an idea for a proof. Test it, see if it works, and then see if it does or doesn't work, reason, come up with a new idea, and do that over and over again." And you can do it all in silicon.

So you know, the results of some of these papers — the proofs — a lot of mathematicians have been talking about them. They call it like an alien intelligence. They don't really understand how the AI connected many different dots, different ideas, different concepts, uh different approaches to solving problems together to actually solve them — that it's very hard for humans to even comprehend how this was done. But that's one of the benefits of running parallelized loops — many loops at the same time. Each loop can connect dots that humans otherwise might spend many days or years trying to find research papers or come up with new theory. And then it can test itself in the compute and come up with the next idea and do it over and over and over again — such that in 3 hours the computer can do the work of hundreds or thousands of years of humans.

Now this is an incredible breakthrough. It's amazing. It's going to change the world in many different ways and it's only the beginning. But it begs the question that I think I need to talk about. If you want to come up with a new drug discovery idea or a new protein folding model or you know solve a problem in chemistry and material science, the loop has a physical component — there's a human in the loop where you actually have to go and test it in a lab. And so there's a slow part of that loop cycle. You can certainly parallelize it. You can come up with better ideas, but the testing — the actual speed of the loop — is actually gated primarily by the physical world step.

Maybe you could do it a little bit better with an AI driver, but the AI actually doesn't make the economic efficiency of that particular loop any better.

Whereas the loops of mathematics — where you come up with an idea, you test it, you realize you're wrong, you test a new idea — which is what mathematicians do as a job, is they're running these loops — that can all be done in silicon in seconds. And if you ask it to solve a problem, it has all of the problems that have previously been solved in its repository — repertoire, if you will — and it is changing everything.

So maybe your thoughts here on Dots, OpenAI, Grokbot, etc. on Dots and Muse and Grokbot.

Chamath：实用主义胜利

I think that what's incredible is you can just turn these things loose on very practical use cases that makes your life better. The best example of this that I saw was just last night in the poker game. Someone was describing to me that they in Grokbot said, "Save me money." And it just kind of like goes through their inbox. It finds all of these different things and it went and canceled a couple of subscriptions and it changed their phone plan and all of a sudden they're saving like a few thousand a year.

So there's these very practical — again, it's just software. If we take out all this philosophical stuff that we started with at the beginning — it's just software and it's very useful software.

So, and by the way, like if you think about how we use it, Jason — you and I — we have, you know, we use Athena. And now Athena is very good because they're like the human concierge that is the elevated version maybe of Grokbot and Dots and Muse, which is like whatever $3,000 a month, but that's my EA layer now.

Yes.

But I still use Grokbot. The combination of Grokbot plus Athena to me is like perfect. So look, there's very tactical and useful measurable utility for very very little money versus what it used to cost. That's an amazing thing.

IP 两天前死了

The more important point I want to make though — I sent this to Nick. There's been a couple things that happened in the last couple days which I think are incredibly important. There have been people that decompiled the entire —

incredible —

the entire Big Five. What is the Big Five? Adobe has five very, very important products in their product suite. Freeberg may know them all, but I just know Photoshop. There's like a bunch of others. Okay.

And these folks decompiled it, distilled it, and published open-source versions of these things. And Rust. Yeah. And I was so shocked because I was like, "Hold on a second. These are like profound products that have existed and have had moats for years and now they're just open-source versions."

And then Nikita was — I think — trolling and he was building on that idea and just talking about GTA because it's about to get released.

Yes,

I think GTA 6 is about to come out and people will reconstruct this.

Why is this important? I think that IP and software was effectively rendered worthless two days ago.

Yes.

Because if you think about it, when everything is headless — so when Elon makes his services headless, Benioff made Salesforce headless a few months earlier — when all of these things are headless and you can wrap them in agent tools and you can connect them via MCP to other experiences, the value of IP does no longer exist in software. It doesn't exist.

And I think that that probably is the most profound implication. So, like even in our business, we would argue with some of our customers all the time because we'll say, "Oh, we'll build this for you. We'll own the IP." They'll say, "No, we want the IP. We don't know how to negotiate it." And two days ago, I walked into the 8090 guys. I said,

"Who cares?"

Who cares?" And —

solve the problem.

But before it was always a negotiation and a set of trade-offs. Now, it's a "who cares" thing where like the IP is irrelevant. It still takes a while for the machinery of a business and frankly the market to understand. But that is the most important thing that happened this weekend in my opinion.

商务层的压缩

I'm going to strongly agree with you and build on it. You have this abstraction of the software layer occurring at the same time, Freeberg, of the abstraction of the website or the marketplace etc.

So now I have like my assistant building Grokbots and then we'll be sharing those. We have it on like a shared account. When we go to make a purchase of something or we try to negotiate something, we're having the agent — without going to any websites — go find all the quotes and then the humans negotiate the second half of it. That's like the sort of perfect option here.

You look at Amazon blocking agents combined with Shopify saying "let's go for it" or Uber and DoorDash are now letting agents go in there and order your burrito or your car. But there's a whole compression of the commerce layer occurring at the same time of the compression of software that Chamath is talking about which will lead to massive deflationary cost savings and speed — the ability to get a hotel room or book a restaurant for an event like I did. This is all being done by bots already.

Freeberg, this could be so deflationary and save people so much money. If people can save 5 or 10% a year on their spending — that's essentially working against or counters the effect of inflation. Yeah, Freeberg.

Freeberg：循环与成为"创造者"

Yeah. Bringing the whole thing full circle. This is kind of what I mentioned earlier on the idea of loops. So think about getting a good price for a hotel. You run a loop which is: check hotel one, look at price. Is it better than current best price? Yes. Okay. It becomes best price. No. Go look for next hotel. And you just run that loop.

And that loop — you can do it in parallel. So you can go run 50 website searches at the exact same time. And you can short-circuit the loop because the software's ability to get that data is faster than the human's ability. So now the loop is: go check 50 websites instantly, give me a result right away. And that's really where the efficiency gain comes from. A loop that gets parallelized, that is done better, and that can be done in a shorter period of time.

I think anything that's done digitally today fits that model. So effectively, all digital workflows are going to get looped. They're going to become more productive. And then the question is how does the human that now levels up leverage all of this loop infrastructure — all these agents — to do more themselves.

I do think — going back to the point earlier that we made about scientists and mathematicians and this challenge for individuals — um mathematicians in particular — I think if your objective historically has been recognition for your work via papers, patents, um —

IP, trademarks, ownership,

IP, yeah, these sorts of things. Um I think that the transition is going to happen which is you're going to have to transition to producing a product. The whole effort of humans — effectively being the loops — because the loops can be digitally automated and scaled and parallelized and so on. I think you end up seeing the necessity for all humans to basically become much more of a maker. You have to make something. You have to do something productive. You have to produce something. You have to provide a service that someone at the end of the day uses or a product that someone at the end of the day consumes — versus just be recognized for your work.

That is the profound shift in society that has to happen and that is going to happen. And I do think people will actually find — I believe this, truly believe all humans have capacity for being producers, for being makers — and all humans will find more joy in their lives in this state versus just getting ribbons for work. Um, and I don't think that it means less money. I think it means more money for all people. Um, more life progress, more prosperity for all people. So, I just zoom out a little bit. And I'm um, you know, I just want to make sure we have that view.

结尾彩蛋：酒店谈判技巧

I think it's a beautiful view of humanity because it's like Jevons paradox. The cheaper things become, the more people can utilize them, the more value they get.

And I hate to — I almost don't want to give this tip because I want to gatekeep it, but I'm going to put it out there anyway. When we book hotels and stuff like that for the team, just get the best prices we can. Then when the human in the loop — we just go to them and say, "Hey, do you have a corporate rate? Can we talk to the manager at the hotel? I know this isn't like super innovative, but hey, can you match this price?" Uh, and all of a sudden, we start saving $1,000 or $2,000 or $3,000 on every hotel.

Say, well, when you have 20 executives moving around the country and you're doing 200 trips a year and you start saving a couple thousand dollar per trip because of this forward motion — like goal-based I guess is sort of what you're saying, Freeberg — like the goal and the outcome is what happens, you can see profound results. And I wouldn't do that myself. But because AI is doing it now — wow, yum yum, it works.

All right. Listen, another amazing episode of the —

I think you're a taker. I don't think you're a maker.

I — what are you talking about, man? All I do — I invest in 100 companies a year. Do you know how hard it is to invest in 100 year-zero startups a year? It is exhausting.

But I must get some lunch. Have you eaten? Do you want to eat lunch?

Yeah. Yeah. Can you come?

I'm so jelly. I'm having FOMO. I'm not with you guys.

All right, everybody. Another amazing episode of your favorite podcast. Your podcast is favorite podcast. The all-in podcast. Love you, boys. Bye-bye.

Bye-bye.

Let your winners ride.

And it said we open-sourced it to the fans and they've just gone crazy with it.

Love you.

Queen of —

besties are my dog taking a notice driveway.

Oh man, my haberdasher will meet me up. We should all just get a room and just have one big huge orgy because they're all just useless. It's like this like sexual tension that we just need to release somehow. Wet your feet. Wet your feet.

Your feet.

We need to get merch. These are going all in. I'm going all in.

item.description:
## 一、表面是宗教争议，本质是软件工程的"命名权"之争
节目最尖锐的洞见其实藏在那句看似随意的话里——Freeberg突然打断："不要用 train，不要用 you，他们是在**编程一个软件**。" 这不是语义洁癖，而是一场**认知战争**的开端。
当 Anthropic 用"Claude 是良心反对者"、"Claude 应该拥有福祉"这种语言写入 Constitution 时，他们并不是在描述软件，而是在**用语言施法**：一旦连工程师自己都用拟人代词来谈论自己的编译产物，监管、伦理、商业谈判的坐标系就全部移位了。这就是维特根斯坦所谓"**语言的边界即世界的边界**"的工业化版本——先占领动词（train vs program），再占领代词（it 变 they），最后现实就不得不跟着代词走。
**出人意料的观察**：Anthropic 真正垄断的不是模型能力，而是**定义模型的那套语言**。GPT-5 可以比 Claude 强，但只要行业继续用"对齐、意识、福祉"这套词汇讨论 AI，Anthropic 就永远占据道德高地上的议程设置者位置。这是一种**语言学意义上的护城河**

item.title: [Alan Chen加州生活号] OpenAI营收风波，AI股急跌又拉回：为什么英伟达没跟上？
item.dc:creator: Alan Chen加州生活号
item.content:encoded:
💡 创造性洞见

一、英伟达"独自掉队"背后的结构性信号——这不是技术面问题

视频里反复追问"为什么 Nvidia 没跟上回弹"，但真正值得警惕的洞察是：它不是被 OpenAI 流言拖累，而是市场正在悄悄完成一次"从卖铲人到淘金者"的坐标系切换。

你看节目中一组反常的组合——Oracle 跌 5% 后反弹、Palantir 创历史新高、Snowflake 持续走强、Palo Alto 把前一天的下杀全部吃回；而 Nvidia 却停在 242 附近、"假突破"。这不是巧合。软件股的 re-rating 从六七月 capitulation 开始，意味着市场终于愿意为"AI 落地的现金流"付溢价，但同时在悄悄降低对"AI 基础设施的无限扩张叙事"的估值乘数。Nvidia 的 PE 和下游应用的 PE 第一次出现了"剪刀差"——这才是 Nvidia 独自走弱的根因，OpenAI 流言只是导火索。

跨领域连接：这幕像极了 1849 年加州淘金潮的后半段。Levi Strauss（卖铲人）的股票初期一骑绝尘，但真正的大牛股是那些建立起稳定销售网络、把矿工收入变成重复消费的零售商。资本市场正在复刻这个剧本：从囤 GPU 的狂热转向"谁能把 token 用量变成账单"的玩家。

二、OpenRouter 的 "250× in 20 months" 隐藏着一个被忽视的二阶效应

节目里丢出一个几乎没被展开的数据——美国 token 使用量从 2025 年 1 月的 0.5 万亿暴涨到 6 月的 1.28 万亿，20 个月 250 倍。大多数评论员会把它读成"AI 不是泡沫"的证据。但真正的洞察藏在二阶导里：

当 token 消费的增长曲线是指数的，网络安全的攻击面也是指数的；但人类监管、补丁、合规的响应能力是线性的。

这意味着嘉宾提到的"几万甚至几百万 agent 同时攻击"不是科幻，而是数学必然。更出人意料的是——这反过来会把 Palo Alto / CrowdStrike 的商业模式结构性拉高一个维度：从席位制（$5000/seat）到 outcome-based + token-metered 的"效用计价"（节目里嘉宾模糊提到了，但没点破要害）。

跨领域连接：这和 19 世纪末电力行业的定价革命一模一样。爱迪生最初卖"灯泡个数"，特斯拉的交流电推动了"kWh 计量计费"的发明——而真正暴涨的不是发电机厂（Nvidia 角色），而是抄表器公司 + 电网运营商（Palo Alto / Cloudflare / CrowdStrike 角色）。网络安全正在经历它的"电表时刻"。

三、一个几乎没人注意到的政治-市场耦合错位

嘉宾顺口提到"中期选举民主党可能翻盘，而民主党选区代表是反数据中心的"，然后立刻说"但市场完全没反应，神奇"。他们把这当作谜题结束，但这恰恰是本周最深的隐藏结构性风险。

VIX 回到交叉区间、周末不对冲、XLF 大阳线突破——这些共同画了一幅图：市场把"降息概率"的权重调到接近 90%，却把"数据中心政治风险"的权重调成 0。两者之间存在定价不一致：如果降息兑现（弱美元 + 流动性），数据中心扩张本应加速；但如果同时政治翻盘，加州/德州/新泽西的 permitting、能源配额、水资源审批会收紧——这是同向利好的货币政策和反向利空的监管政策同时被忽略了后者。

出人意料的观察：Nvidia 没跟上回弹，可能不仅是估值问题，还是少数几家对冲基金已经在悄悄 price in 这个政治风险。你观察到的"murderer light"反复砸盘、"假突破后无法立足"，更像是聪明钱提前对冲中期选举的 data center backlash，而非散户对 OpenAI 流言的过度反应。

四、Palantir 的 "2000+ forward-deployed engineers" 其实是解盘密码

节目一笔带过，但这个数字惊人——Palantir 不是 SaaS 公司，它是披着 SaaS 外壳的高级咨询公司。这解释了两件事：

  1. 为什么 Michael Burry 用传统 SaaS 估值模型做空它必输：他看到的是 60× P/S，但没看到每个 FDE 背后锁定的是政府/财富 500 强的五年期合约，这些合约的续约率和 Accenture 更像，而非 Snowflake。
  2. 为什么 Palantir 的 AI 落地叙事可信度最高：有 2000 个工程师直接驻场客户现场，等于拥有最大的真实世界 agent 部署数据集——这是 OpenAI 和 Anthropic 都买不到的 moat。

跨领域连接：这个模式其实源自 1960s 的 IBM——当年 IBM 的 System/360 之所以统治企业市场，不是因为硬件好，而是因为每笔销售附带驻场工程师团队。Palantir 几乎原封不动地复制了这个"硬件时代的服务护城河 → AI 时代的落地护城河"的模板。市场正在重新发现这件事，于是给出历史新高。

…not to mention the internet security, which is often talked about, after the news of the internet security yesterday, it was also taken away. In addition, NET's financial reporting, half of the data is about the data of robots and AI agents. These factors can give everyone good information that AI is not a bubble. Now many scenarios are applying AI. More and more agents. The demand for network security is growing.

Think about it. You used to be a hacker. You might write scripts or something. Your scale is not as exaggerated as it is now. You are always attacking several times. Or one point. I'm not a hacker. But this may be wrong. But I think the scale of the previous hacker attacks should be smaller. Now you make a AI agent's army, maybe tens of thousands, or even millions of agents, attacking at the same time, seems to be much easier than before. Now, for the safety of the Internet, you have to —

In the future, it may become a chair of $5,000. Then add your AI add-on $10,000. AI token usage, add $10,000 to you. Then the outcome-based bonus, add $5,000 to you. The original $10,000 a month becomes $20,000, $30,000, $35,000 a month. So now its pricing is getting more and more complicated. In the future, it's definitely not like the IT environment we were in before. It's just so simple. Very small-scale attacks. And software is also very simple. Things will be very complicated in the future.

So I think the main line of network security, don't think that the main line of network security is over after a few days of being popular. It's over. I think it's just the beginning.

九、软件股 Re-rating：Snowflake、Palantir 与"从卖铲到应用"切换

In addition to the security of the network, the software version is actually good in the whole version. I remember whether we drew the downward trend line in this picture last week or the week before, or where we drew it in the member's question. This is what I drew before. Today you can see that there is also a possible transaction volume on Friday. This is a breakthrough that continues to create new high.

We also mentioned several key leaders of software stocks, including Snow. We analyzed Snow's first high gap-up, and it went all the way to the long red, which is the trend of new highs. Palantir also created a new high today, which should be a historical high. You can see that this is the peak of software stocks at that time. When they first gap-up the financial report — very strong.

Before, the software was dead. Do you remember? In the first half of the year, this was the biggest trend. In the second half of the year, you can see that software is gradually getting stronger. The hardware is a little bit softer. But it's not bad. So I think that in the future, software stocks still have a chance. You can find some leaders in the whole IGV version, find some angels who have fallen or haven't yet grown. We can do more analysis on the member channel. But if you have the ability, you can also find good landmarks here.

Do you remember Palantir? Who said he should be a go-getter? Michael Berry. He still has the empty seat. The data he has now is delayed, but he has not released it yet. According to his little articles, he did not say that he has already shut down the empty seat of Palantir. Now it's all exposed. The chrysanthemum is already in the body. The flesh is already blurred. So I don't know. I always laugh at him. But I've been watching Palantir getting higher and higher. Now it's all-time high. Even if he's only 5 or 6 years old, he'll still lose even after 10 years. He can't just sit there and wait 10 years for the next position.

Yes, Palantir's position — I think the logic of trading, including the next logic of the market, will certainly start to turn to AI applications. Before, these things could not make money or it was difficult to have continuous profit. But now in the market, obviously, after the capitulation in June and July, especially after this big financial storm, the market has obviously given it a new price, a new valuation, called re-rating. Snow, Palantir, Microsoft, and many other software companies are all going through this process. In the first half of the year, they were scolded, they were smashed, and they were sprayed. In the second half of the year, including the beginning of next year, they will be doing great. Now, they can start to get some momentum, right?

Do you know a data that Palantir is the company with the most forward-deployed engineers in the entire technology industry? I don't know. It's the most, it's more than 2,000.

十、Microsoft / Adobe 禁令、印度话题与员工结构

And then, recently, these software companies, there was a news yesterday, Microsoft and Adobe have been banned from selling. Yes, this is the vice president's comment. Yes, mainly for Indians. Yes, yes, yes.

Do you remember our joke? The female AI is actually called "Actually Indian". And today my client asked me what does "s-i" mean? I said "Surely Indian". Yes, India is also in a mess recently. If you follow my Instagram, I post more posts about India. I always win the controversy.

I don't know if Palantir has a lot of R3 companies. Yes, there are quite a lot of Indian employees in these tech companies. The news should not have a big impact on them.

十一、SpaceX 走强、Starlink 与印度电信博弈

Speaking of India, let's talk about SpaceX. In May, we talked about SpaceX. I discussed it with Will. My opinion was that SpaceX performed well. On Monday, it rose 7% crazily. On Monday, it rose to $176. The market value was $2.5 trillion. It was a strong trend.

SpaceX has some big news this week. One is Starlink to provide satellite signals. This is a good example. Another example is that Musk also took this opportunity to spray the Indian telecommunications company, also called Armani. He is an Indian telecommunications head of the Indian market. He said, "We applied for a license and a contract. Why haven't you approved it for so long? Is there some trouble?"

Of course, India is a head of the telecommunications industry. That widow has a beautiful daughter, right? Anyway, her family lives in a big building. All of them are her relatives. And hundreds of servants serve them. This is his son. He's fat. But if I see on the app, I don't know if it's a human or a machine, saying publicly, "Mask, how can you enter India? We don't welcome you. We have our own beliefs. We have our own communications. We have our own good social media. I want to cancel your access. I want to quit."

It doesn't feel like a normal reaction from the people. It's more like a — I was impressed by the character of the character. She is a beautiful girl. When she was in her wedding, Rihanna flew over to perform for her. I know what you mean.

十二、国债收益率、消费端走弱与 Nike 的产品困境

We have 5 minutes left. Let's look at the national debt revenue. The national debt revenue this Thursday and Friday can actually see that there are some solid or slow-moving forms. It didn't continue to hit new highs, but the interest rate of the mortgage seems to hit a new high. It seems to be higher than 7.5 in 30 years. This is quite a big impact on consumers or the actual economy.

We also saw Walmart starting to jump. Right, interesting. There are some negative comments, you can pay attention to that. There are a lot of sales.

Oh, and Victoria's Secret. I forgot the ticker, it means I'm a very honest person. I don't know either. I think the ticker is… it should be sexy. Vsexy, right? Oh, I think so. Why can't I find it? It seems to be VSXY. VSXY, that's right. This picture is really beautiful.

Nike is still quite poor. Nike is another story. Nike is a product that was designed by itself. Yes, yes, yes. How to say, Nike, Lululemon, after changing people, its design has never been anything new. And the surface, its performance is not very good.

Nike, this is a very important thing, is that its sneaker has not been innovative for many years. No new platform has been released. Interesting.

I forgot what the ticker is. It's ONON. Oh hey, he still looks a bit like this — the lake is pretty beautiful. You don't say. Yes, he is the most — Nike's one is a pool of water. But his hand is also fine recently. Of course all the shoes are not so good. Yes, yes, yes, yes. But Nike is particularly poor, his financial report is not so good. Everyone is here before that. There is a — before, Nike is very dependent on the Chinese market. Foreign situation…
